image-based modeling and render in computer graphic and computer vision image-based modeling and rendering ibmr method rely on a set of two-dimensional image of a scene to generate a three-dimensional model and then render some novel view of this scene the traditional approach of computer graphic have be use to create a geometric model in 3d and try to reproject it onto a two-dimensional image computer vision conversely be mostly focus on detect group and extract feature edge face etc. present in a give picture and then try to interpret they as three-dimensional clue image-based modeling and rendering allow the use of multiple two-dimensional image in order to generate directly novel two-dimensional image skip the manual modeling stage instead of consider only the physical model of a solid ibmr method usually focus more on light modeling the fundamental concept behind ibmr be the plenoptic illumination function which be a parametrisation of the light field the plenoptic function describe the light ray contain in a give volume it can be represent with seven dimension a ray be define by its position formula_1 its orientation formula_2 its wavelength formula_3 and its time formula_4 formula_5 ibmr method try to approximate the plenoptic function to render a novel set of two-dimensional image from another give the high dimensionality of this function practical method place constraint on the parameter in order to reduce this number typically to to image-based modeling • projective method these technique exploit projective property of the scene to reconstruct geometric model directly from a set of photograph photo3d photomodeler photobuilder • tour into the picture tour into the picture the simplest image-based modeling technique recover from a single picture a extremely simplify scene model consist of just a few texture-mapped polygon • Façade The Façade system use a non-linear optimization algorithm to reconstruct 3d textured model of architectural element from photograph • Voxel color the algorithm identify a special set of invariant voxel which together form a spatial and photometric reconstruction of the scene able to cope with large change in visibility and its modeling of intrinsic scene color and texture information fully consistent with the input image • multi-view geometry it be a set of intricate geometric relation between multiple view of a 3d scene apply to recover 3d model from image image-based rendering ibr • light-field render it be a method for generate new view from arbitrary camera position without depth information or feature matching simply by combine and resample the available image • plenoptic stitch it give the viewer the ability to explore unobstructed environment of arbitrary size and shape use appropriate sampling for most viewpoint in the environment by move omnidirectional video camera over the grid • cylindrical panorama it provide horizontal orientation independence when explore a environment from a single point cylindrical panorama can be create use specialize panoramic camera • concentric mosaic it be a generalization of cylindrical panorama that allow the viewer to explore a circular region and experience horizontal parallax and lighting effect in this case instead of use a single cylindrical image slit camera be rotate along planar concentric circle a series of concentric manifold mosaic be create by compose the slit image acquire by each camera along they circular path unlike light field and lumigraph where camera be place on a two-dimensional grid the concentric mosaic representation reduce the amount of datum by capture a sequence of image along a circle path • Lumigraph it be similar to light field render but it apply approximate geometry to compensate for non-uniform sampling in order to improve render performance • transfer method they be characterize by the use of a relatively small number of image with the application of geometric constraint either recover at some stage or know a priori to reproject image pixel appropriately at a give virtual camera viewpoint laveau and faugeras • Relief texture to improve the render speed of 3d warping the warping process be factored into a relatively simple pre-warping step and a traditional texture mapping step • image-based object they provide a compact image-based representation for 3d object that can be render in occlusion-compatible order a image-based object be construct by acquire multiple view of the object register and resample they from every center of projection onto the face of a parallelepiped the use of a parallelepiped allow such a representation to be decompose into parameterized planar region for which a warper can be efficiently implement • image-based visual hull it be base on efficient computation and shade visual hull from silhouette image datum the algorithm take advantage of epipolar geometry and incremental computation to achieve a constant rendering cost per render pixel • 3d warp with available depth information for every point in one or more image 3d warping technique can be use to render from any nearby point of view by project the pixel of the original image to they proper 3d location and re-project they onto the new picture • layered depth image to deal with the disocclusion artifact in 3d warping layered depth image be propose to store not only what be visible in the input image but also what be behind the visible surface each pixel in the input image contain a list of depth and color value where the ray from the pixel intersect with the scene • view-dependent texture map view-dependent texture mapping be use to render novel view by warp and composit several input image a three-step view-dependent texture mapping method be consider to further reduce the computational cost and provide smoother blending this method employ visibility preprocessing polygon-view map and projective texture mapping • surface light field it be a function that assign a color to each ray originate on a surface surface light field be well suit to construct virtual image of shiny object under complex lighting condition • light field map this method be a representation and interactive visualization of surface light field by partition the radiance datum over elementary surface primitive and by approximate each partition datum by a small set of lower-dimensional discrete function the render algorithm decode directly from this compact representation at interactive frame rate for a exhaustive overview of the currently available popularity in all region of Brazil Forró be closely associate with brazilian June Festivals which celebrate a number of Christian saint the most celebrated be Saint John day there be several theory on Forró rabecado where the accordion be replace by a fiddle the triangle keep a ongoing pulse on all the four time of the beat while accentuate the third beat in this sense the function can be compare Haplodiploidy Haplodiploidy be a sex-determination system in which male develop from unfertilized egg and be haploid and female develop from fertilize egg and be diploid Haplodiploidy be sometimes call arrhenotoky Haplodiploidy determine the sex in all member of the insect order hymenoptera bee ant and wasp and thysanoptera thrips the system also occur sporadically in some spider mite Hemiptera Coleoptera bark beetle and rotifer in this system sex be determine by the number of set of chromosome a individual receive a offspring form from the union of a sperm and a egg develop as a female and a unfertilized egg develop as a male this mean that the male have half the number of chromosome that a female have and be haploid the haplodiploid sex-determination system have a number of peculiarity for example a male have no father and can not have son but he have a grandfather and can have grandson additionally if a eusocial-insect colony have only one queen and she have only mate once then the relatedness between worker diploid female in a hive or nest be this mean the worker in such monogamous single-queen colony be significantly more closely related than in other sex determination system where the relatedness of sibling be usually no more than it be this point which drive the kin selection theory of how eusociality evolve whether haplodiploidy do in fact pave the way for the evolution of eusociality be still a matter of debate another feature of the haplodiploidy system be that recessive lethal and deleterious allele will be remove from the population rapidly because they will automatically be express in the male dominant lethal and deleterious allele be remove from the population every time they arise as they kill any individual they arise in Haplodiploidy be not the same thing as a x0 sex-determination system in haplodiploidy male receive one half of the chromosome that female receive include autosome in a x0 sex-determination system male and female receive a equal number of autosome but when it come to sex chromosome female will receive two x chromosome while male will receive only a single x chromosome several model have be propose for the genetic mechanism of haplodiploid sex-determination the model most commonly refer to be the complementary allele model accord to this model if a individual be heterozygous for a certain locus it develop into a female whereas hemizygous and homozygous individual develop into male in other word diploid offspring develop from fertilize egg and be normally female while haploid offspring develop into male from unfertilized egg diploid male would be infertile as they cell would not undergo meiosis to form sperm therefore the sperm would be diploid which mean that they offspring would be triploid since hymenopteran mother and son share the same gene they may be especially sensitive to inbreeding Inbreeding reduce the number of different sex allele present in a population hence increase the Pinyin input method the pinyin method refer to a family of input method base on the pinyin method of romanization in the most basic form the pinyin method allow a user to input chinese character by enter the pinyin of a chinese character and then present the user with a list of possible character with that pronunciation however there be a number of slightly different such system in use and modern pinyin method provide a number of convenient feature the obvious advantage of pinyin-based input method be the ease of learn for Standard Chinese speaker those who be familiar with pinyin would be able to input chinese character with almost no training compare to other input method for people who do not speak Chinese the main advantage of pinyin become its disadvantage they will need to learn the Standard Chinese pronunciation of character before they be able to use this input method however since all child in Mainland China be require to learn pinyin in school pinyin be in fact very popular there unlike stroke-based input method the pinyin method only require the user to know how to speak Mandarin and be able to recognize the character it do not require the user to be able to construct the character from scratch as one would do in write chinese this be both a advantage and a disadvantage it be a advantage in that people will be able to type all the character they can recognize it be a disadvantage in that it may cause language attrition and skill loss in adult and it may be a learning barrier for write chinese in child Pinyin input method differ in a number of possible aspect most pinyin input method provide convenience feature to speed up input some of these feature can speed up typing immensely the basic idea of a input method be to have a buffer that hold the user input until it be convert into character that would otherwise be unavailable from the keyboard in the most basic system one character be convert at a time this make a very time consuming input process not only do the user have to select character one at a time it also mean that the input system do not have the ability to prioritize character choice use word phrase grammatical structure or context in addition since the input method only support one character at a time it likely require the user to type out the full pinyin spelling to narrow down the selection this system still exist in embedded application such as cell phone common pinyin implementation on the computer today can hold up to a clause in pinyin before require a conversion the method attempt to guess the appropriate character by use word phrase from a dictionary grammatical structure and context chinese be a tonal language tone can be use to further distinguish character of the same sound many of the early single-character pinyin method implementation require input of tone in order to narrow down the character selection for the sake of convenience tone selection be disable by default in most modern pinyin system on the computer the user may have the option to enable it depend on the pinyin implementation with the exception of intonation there be two extended latin vowel in pinyin they be ü u-umlaut and ê e-circumflex give that the keyboard layout be the most common keyboard layout in China any pinyin method implementation would need to be able to facilitate the input of those vowel on date and time notation in Africa in many east african language the start of the daily time system be at dawn not midnight thus what would be seven o'clock in the morning in English become one o'clock in the morning in Swahili and other east african language this also affect the date the whole night be the same date as the precede day for example Tuesday do not become Wednesday until morning break rather than change at midnight for multi-lingual speaker in East Africa the convention be to use the time system applicable to the language one happen to be speak at the time a person speaking of a early morning event in English would report that it happen at eight o'clock however in repeat the same fact in Swahili one would state that the event occur at saa mbilus two hour the Ganda form ssawa bbiri be equivalent to the Swahili in that it mean literally two hour

be measure use a pressure transducer with the pressure information be subsequently send to the vehicle to warn the driver of under or over inflation of a tire the pressure information be commonly gear and gear rack the process be perform on gasher or universal milling machine especially in the case of worm wheel after gash the gear or sprocket be finish via hobbing shaping or shaving Gashers be large heavy-duty machine tool they have horizontal and vertical slideway precise indexing large diameter ballscrew and spindle drive motor up to they be usually control via computer numerical control cnc or a microprocessor while they be usually use for rough cutting they be also sometimes use for finish for example gasher be use for the production of large roller-chain sprocket gash be first use to rough out worm wheel use a universal milling machine but then dedicate gasher be build to rough out other type of gear because the process be carry out on two different machine the process differ the process use a milling cutter with a cross-section that be slightly smaller than the final cross-section of the cut it have the same diameter as the worm the cutter be then angle to the gash angle the gash angle be calculate from the lead and pitch diameter of the worm often table be available with the gash angle for common diameter and lead the cutter be center over the blank and then plunge into it to the proper depth the cutter be finally withdraw and the blank index to the next tooth space and cut this be repeat until all of the tooth space have be cut note that a standard endmill with round corner can be use instead if a special milling cutter be unavailable the endmill should be the pitch diameter note that be process can not be use on a small worm wheel that where the sugar cane plant be domesticate Sugar cane probably originate in Papua New Guinea and from there be take to Southeast Asia and other Pacific Islands and ultimately to India and China from India sugar spread to the Arab state and eventually to Europe chemically sugar candy be broadly divide into two group crystalline candy and amorphous candy crystalline candy be not as hard as crystal of the mineral variety but derive they name and they texture from they microscopically organize sugar structure form through a process of crystallization which make they easy to bite or cut into fudge cream and fondant be example of crystalline candy amorphous candy have a disorganized crystalline structure they usually have higher sugar concentration and the texture may be chewy hard or brittle hard candy such as lollipop caramel nut brittle and toffee be all example of amorphous candy even though some of they be as hard as rock and resemble crystal in they overall appearance crystalline candy be chemically describe as have two phase because the tiny solid sugar crystal be suspend in a thick liquid solution these be also call grain candy because they can have a grainy texture amorphous candy be have only one phase which be either solid or liquid and do not have a grainy texture so they may be call ungrained commercially candy be often divide into three group accord to the amount of sugar they contain each of these three group contain both crystalline grain and amorphous ungrained candy Historically sugar candy be use for pharmaceutical preparation as well as food use the sugar candy be use to disguise the unpleasant taste of the drug ingredient cough sweet and some other drug show this heritage in the form of sugar tablet contain drug active drug ingredient be add to hard candy and pan sugar coating surround unpalatable pill shelf life be largely determine by the amount of water present in the candy and the storage condition high-sugar candy such as hard candy can have a shelf life of many year if keep cover in a dry environment Spoilage for low-moisture sugar candy tend to involve a loss of shape color texture and flavor rather than the growth of dangerous microbe impermeable packaging can reduce spoilage due to storage condition Sugar candy spoil more quickly if they have different amount of water in different part of the candy for example a candy that combine marshmallow and nougat or if they be store in high-moisture environment this process be due to the effect of water activity which result in the transfer of unwanted water from a high-moisture environment into a low-moisture candy render it rubbery or the loss of desirable water from a high-moisture candy into a dry environment render the candy dry and brittle another factor affect only non-crystalline amorphous sugar candy be the glass transition process this can cause amorphous sugar candy to lose they intended texture

eaves the eaves be the edge of the roof which overhang the face of a wall and normally project beyond the side of a building the eaves form a overhang to throw water clear of the wall and may be highly decorate as part of a architectural style such as the chinese dougong bracket system eaves be derive from Old English mean edge accord to the Oxford English Dictionary eave be both the singular and plural form of the word however the Merriam-Webster website list the word as eave and state that it be usually use in plural the word be use before the 12th century in the form efes Old English the primary function of the eaves be to keep rain water off the wall and to prevent the ingress of water at the junction where the roof meet the wall the eaves may also protect a pathway around the building from the rain prevent erosion of the footing and reduce splatter on the wall from rain as it hit the ground the secondary function be to control solar penetration as a form of passive solar building design the eaves overhang can be design to adjust the building solar gain to suit the local climate the latitude and orientation of the building the eaves overhang may also shelter opening to ventilate the roof space aesthetic traditional or purely decorative consideration may prevail over the strictly functional requirement of the eaves the art and Crafts Movement influence the american craftsman tradition which have very wide eaves with decorative bracket for which there be not necessarily a real functional need likewise the italian style eave show above the eaves may terminate in a fascia a board run the length of the eaves under the tile or roof sheet to cap off and protect the expose rafter end and to provide grounds on which to fix gutter at the gable the eaves may extend beyond the gable end wall by project the purlin and be usually cap off by bargeboard to protect the wall and the purlin end the underside of the eaves may be fill with a horizontal soffit fix at right angle to the wall the soffit may be decorative but it also have the function of seal the gap between the rafter from vermin and weather eaves must be design for local wind speed as the overhang can significantly increase the wind load on the roof the line on the ground under the outer edge of the eaves be the eavesdrip or dripline and in typical building planning regulation define the extent of the building and can not oversail the property boundary

the probability of specific element although the concept have be vaguely discuss in various form for some time it be generally attribute to Richard von Mises who use the term collective rather than sequence intuitively speak the principle state that it be not possible to select a sub-sequence of a random sequence in a way to improve the odds for a specific event for instance if a coin toss sequence be random with equal and independent chance for head and tail then bet on head every 3rd 7th or 21st toss etc. do not change the odds of win in the long run Richard von Mises liken the principle of the impossibility of a gambling system to the principle of the conservation of energy a law that can not be prove but have hold true in repeat experiment elsewhere von Mises have also also not bias the sub-sequence selection criterion impose by von Mises be important because although be not bias by select the odd position we get which be not random Von Mises never totally formalize he definition of a proper selection rule for sub-sequence but in Alonzo Church define it as any recursive function which have read the first n element of the sequence decide if it want to select element number n +1 Church be a pioneer in the field of computable function and the definition he make rely on the Church Turing Thesis for computability in the mid a. Kolmogorov and Loveland independently propose a more permissive selection rule in they view Church recursive function definition be too restrictive in that it read the element in order instead they propose a rule base on a partially computable process which have read any n element of the sequence decide if it want to select another element which have not be read yet the principle influence modern concept in randomness e.g. the work by a. ramp up ramp up be a term use in economics and business to describe a increase in firm production ahead of anticipated increase in product demand alternatively ramp up describe the period from complete initial product development to maximum capacity utilization characterize by product and process experimentation and improvement ramp up in the first sense often occur when a company strike a deal with a distributor retailer or producer which will substantially increase product demand for example in June after launch a joint venture with Guangzhou Automobile Toyota announce that it would ramp up production in China to meet expected increase in market demand by construct a plant in Guangdong which would produce some additional Camry sedan in the consumer electronics industry manufacturer often ramp up production in the early fall to meet demand during the holiday selling season as ramp up be typical in early stage of firm or market development the term and process be widely associate with venture capital which seek to rapidly increase rate of return on investment just prior to exit for example wrightspeed the producer of the x1 electric car prototype begin to seek out capital in order to hire on well-trained employee in order to ramp up production in anticipation of sale success

Gyrochronology Gyrochronology be a method for estimate the age of a low-mass star like the Sun from its rotation period the term be derive from the greek word gyro chrono and logo roughly translate as rotation age and study respectively it be coin in by Sydney Barnes to describe the associate procedure for derive stellar age and develop extensively in empirical form in the technique build on a insight of Andrew Skumanich who realize that another measure of stellar rotation v sin i decline steadily with stellar age Gyrochronology use the rotation period p of the star instead of the doubly ambiguous v sin i which depend on the unknown inclination of the star axis of rotation i in particular the technique account for the substantial mass dependence of stellar rotation as exemplify by early rotation-period work on the Hyades open cluster these two improvement be largely responsible for the precision in the age provide by gyrochronology the associate age estimate for a star be know as the gyrochronological age the basic idea underlie gyrochronology be that the rotation period p of a main-sequence cool star be a deterministic function of its age t and its mass m or a suitable proxy such as color the detailed dependency of rotation be such that the period converge rapidly to a certain function of age and mass mathematically denote by p p t m even though star have a range of allow initial period consequently cool star do not occupy the entire 3-dimensional parameter space of mass age period but instead define a 2-dimensional surface in this space therefore measure two of these variable yield the third of these quantity the mass or a proxy such as color and the rotation period be the easier variable to measure provide access to the star age otherwise difficult to obtain define a star as sun-like be very difficult because to be sun-like the star should have a mass radius age temperature metallicity and spectral type that be similar to the Sun measure most of these factor be difficult and determine the age of a star be extremely difficult so astronomer tend to ignore it when decide if a star be sun-like or not however this be not ideal because the Sun and all star change over time if a star rotation period be less than day the star can be determine as be younger than the Sun if the rotation rate be longer the star can be determine as be older than the Sun the relationship between rotation and age be initially discover by Soren Meibom and colleague by measure the period of rotation of star in a billion-year-old cluster because the age of the star be already know the researcher could discover a relationship between a star age and its rotation period a study of cool star in the 2.5-billion-year-old cluster allow to estimate the age period relationship for older star use these result the age of a large number of cool galactic field star can be derive with % precision

random-looking sequence of coin toss they tend to make sequence where the proportion of head to tail stay closer to in any short segment than would be predict by chance insensitivity to sample size Kahneman and Tversky interpret this to mean that people believe short sequence of random event should be representative of longer one the representativeness heuristic be also cite behind the related phenomenon of the clustering illusion accord to which people see streak of random event as be non-random when such streak be actually much more likely to occur in small sample than people expect the Crossover study a crossover study also refer to as a crossover trial be a longitudinal study in which subject receive a sequence of different treatment or exposure while crossover study can be observational study many important crossover study be control experiment which be discuss in this article crossover design be common for experiment in many scientific discipline for example psychology pharmaceutical science and medicine randomize control crossover experiment be especially important in health care in a randomize clinical trial the subject be randomly assign to different arm of the study which receive different treatment when the randomize clinical trial be a repeat measure design the same measure be collect multiple time for each subject a crossover clinical trial be a repeat measure design in which each patient be assign to a sequence of treatment include at least two treatment of which one treatment may be a standard treatment or a placebo nearly all crossover design have balance which mean that all subject should receive the same number of treatment and that all subject participate for the same number of period in most crossover trial in fact each subject receive all treatment statistician suggest that design have four period a design which allow study to be truncate to three period while still enjoy greater efficiency than the two-period design however the two-period design be often teach in non-statistical textbook partly because of its simplicity the datum be analyze use the statistical method that be specify in the clinical trial protocol which need to have be approve by the appropriate institutional review board and regulatory agency before the trial could begin again the clinical trial protocol specify the method of statistical analysis most clinical trial be analyze use repeated-measurements anova analysis of variance or mixed model that include random effect in most longitudinal study of human subject patient may withdraw from the trial or become lose to follow-up due e.g. to move abroad or to die from another disease there be statistical method for deal with such missing-data and censor problem a important method analyze the datum accord to the principle of the intention to treat a crossover study have two advantage over both a parallel study and a non-crossover longitudinal study first the influence of confounding covariate be reduce because each crossover patient serve as he or she own control in a non-crossover study even randomize it be often the case that different treatment-group be find to be unbalanced on some covariate in a control randomize crossover design such imbalance be implausible unless covariate be to change systematically during the study second optimal crossover design be statistically efficient and so require fewer subject than do non-crossover design even other repeat measure design optimal crossover design be discuss in the graduate textbook by Jones and Kenward and in the review article by Stufken crossover design be discuss along with more general repeated-measurement design in the graduate textbook by Vonesh and Chinchilli these study be often do to improve the symptom of patient with chronic condition for curative treatment or rapidly change condition cross-over trial may be infeasible or unethical crossover study often have two problem First be the issue of order effect because it be possible that the order in which treatment be administer may affect the outcome a example might be a drug with many adverse effect give first make patient take a second less harmful medicine more sensitive to any adverse effect Second be the issue of carry-over between treatment which confound the estimate of the treatment effect in practice carry-over effect can be avoid with a sufficiently long wash-out period between treatment however plan for sufficiently long wash-out period require expert knowledge of the dynamics of the treatment which be often unknown also there might be a learning effect this be important where you have control who be naive to the intended therapy in such a case e.g. you can not make a group typically the group which learn the skill first unlearn a skill such as yoga and then act as a control in the second phase of the study

subject of a Harvard Business Review summary in natural capitalism the author describe the global economy as be dependent on natural resource and ecosystem service that nature provide natural capitalism be a critique of traditional Industrial capitalism say that the traditional system of capitalism do not fully conform to its own accounting principle it liquidate its capital and call it income it neglect to assign any value to the largest stock of capital it employ the natural resource and live system as well as the social and cultural system that be the basis of human capital natural capitalism recognize the critical interdependency between the production and use of human-made capital and the maintenance and supply of natural capital the author argue that only through recognize this essential relationship with the Earth valuable resource can business and the people they support continue to exist they fundamental question be what would a economy look like if it fully value all form of capital what if a economy be organize not around the abstraction of neoclassical economics and accountancy but around the biological reality of nature what if generally accept accounting principle recognize natural and human capital not as a free amenity in inexhaustible supply but as a finite and integrally valuable factor of production what if in the absence of a rigorous way to practice such accounting company start to act as if such principle be in force the author of natural capitalism say that these choice be possible and such a economy would offer a stunning new set of opportunity for all of society amount to no less than the next industrial revolution the book have many practical suggestion for company interest in a sustainable future accord to the author the next industrial revolution depend on the espousal of four central strategy the conservation of resource through more effective manufacturing process the reuse of material as find in natural system a change in value from quantity to quality and invest in natural capital or restore and sustain natural resource while traditional industrial capitalism primarily recognize the value of money and goods as capital natural capitalism extend recognition to natural capital and human capital problem such as pollution and social injustice may then be see as failure to properly account for capital rather than as inherent failure of capitalism itself the fundamental assumption of natural capitalism be as follow in a interview Paul Hawken describe he motivation behind the title natural capitalism he state that it be intend to be a pun on natural capital a term originally coin by Schumacher in hawken endorse the underlie concept of natural capital and its implication for society so add a - ism at the end of that word as a double entendre despite this intention from Hawken many reader interpret this wordplay in the opposite way there be dissent from reader who misunderstand the title believe process not involve or require human activity Artificiality often carry with it the implication of be false counterfeit or deceptive the philosopher Aristotle write in he Rhetoric however intelligence political scientist and artificial intelligence expert Herbert Simon observe that some artificial thing be imitation of thing in nature and the imitation may use either the same basic material as those in the natural object or quite different material Simon distinguish between the artificial and the synthetic the former be a imitation of something find in nature for example a artificial sweetener which generate sweetness use a formula not find in nature and the latter be a replication of something find in nature for example a sugar create in a laboratory that be chemically indistinguishable from a naturally occur sugar some philosopher have go further and assert that in a deterministic world everything be natural and nothing be artificial because everything in the world include everything make by human be a product of the physical law of the world it be generally possible for human and in some instance for computer to distinguish natural from artificial environment the artificial environment tend to have more physical regularity both spatially and over time with natural environment tend to have both irregular structure and structure that change over time however on close observation it be possible to discern some mathematical structure and pattern in natural environment which can then be replicate to create a artificial environment with a more natural culture of Eritrea the culture of Eritrea be the collective cultural heritage of the various population native to Eritrea it share historic commonality with the tradition of Ethiopia Somalia Djibouti and Sudan the local culture consist of various and often quite similar tradition practice by the nation many cushitic and ethiopian semitic-speaking afro-asiatic ethnic group in addition to those practice by the area nilotic minority one of the most recognizable part of eritrean culture be the coffee ceremony Coffee Ge'ez ቡን būn be offer when visit friend during festivity or as a daily staple of life if coffee be politely decline then most likely tea shaus ሻሂ shahee will be serve the coffee be brew by first roast the green coffee bean over hot coal gughin a brazier once the bean be roasted of the bean traditionally in a wooden mortar and pestle the coffee grounds be then put into a special vessel call a jebena and boil a jebena be usually make of clay and have a spherical base a neck and pour spout and a handle where the neck connect with the base when the coffee boil up through the neck it be pour in and out of another container to cool it and then be put back into the jebena until it happen again to pour the coffee from the jebena a filter make from horsehair or other material be place in the spout of the jebena to prevent the grounds from escape the host pour the coffee for all participant by move the tilted jebena over a tray with small handleless cup finjal without stop until each cup be full some of the coffee will inevitably miss the cup but this be do to prevent the coffee grounds from contaminate the brew one extra cup be pour each time the grounds be brew four time the first round of coffee be call awel the second kale'i the third bereka to be bless and the fourth be call dereja however the dereja be not always pour it be mostly pour when elder be present the coffee ceremony may also include burning of various traditional incense such as frankincense or gum arabic typically eritrean cuisine consist of various stew tsebhus make from vegetable and meat and serve atop a large flat sourdough bread call injera tayta shuro alicha and hamly many vegetarian dish be available since a majority of the population observe fasting at some time during the year Eating be accomplish without utensil by tear a piece of injera strictly use the right hand then scoop some stew vegetable or salad with the bread on visit a eritrean household it be polite to decline at least three time if ask to dine usually the host will say bezay kelalem after which the guest may agree to dine this process ensure that one do not seem too eager to eat at another household when one visit a eritrean house regardless of whether they be serve with food or not they be always serve with hot tea Eritrea have nine ethnic group each of which have they own different style of music and accompany dance a common instrument use by many of the community be the drum amongst the help be its verifiability quantifiability consistency and objectivity the development and application of a trading strategy follow eight step Formulation specification in computer-testable form preliminary testing optimization evaluation of performance and robustness trading of the strategy monitoring of trading performance refinement and evolution for every trading strategy one need to define asset to trade entry/exit point and money management rule bad money management can make a potentially profitable strategy unprofitable trading strategy be base on fundamental or technical analysis or engage they both Technical strategy can be broadly divide into the mean-reversion and momentum group there be also specific strategy like sell in May and go away but remember to get back in September trading strategy be usually verify by backtest where the process should follow the scientific method and by forward testing a.k.a. paper trading where they be test in a simulated trading environment momentum signal e.g. 52-week high have be show to be successful in trading strategy and be use by financial analyst in they buy and sell recommendation the term trading strategy can in brief be use by any fixed plan of trade a financial instrument but the general use of the term be within computer assist trading where a trading strategy be implement as computer program for automate trading the trading strategy be develop by the follow method usually the performance of a trading strategy be measure on the risk-adjusted basis probably the most known risk-adjusted performance measure be the Sharpe ratio however in practice one usually compare the expect return against the volatility of return or the maximum drawdown normally higher expect return imply higher volatility and drawdown the choice of the risk-reward trade-off strongly depend on trader risk preference often the performance be measure against a benchmark the most common one be a exchange-traded fund on a stock for either conservative or aggressive trading style

Ningyōtsukai or Ningyōzukai puppeteer the Tayū chanter and shamisen musician occasionally other instrument such as taiko drum will be use the most accurate term for the traditional puppet theater in Japan be the combination of chant and shamisen playing be call jōruri and the japanese word for puppet or doll generally be ningyō it be use in many play Bunraku puppetry have be a document traditional activity for japanese people for hundred of year Bunraku history go as far back as the 16th century but the origin of the modern form can be trace to the it rise to popularity after the sophisticated mechanically in play with supernatural theme a puppet may be construct so that its face can quickly transform into that of a demon less complex head may have eye that move up and down Automatic bug fix Automatic bug-fixing be the automatic repair of software bug without the intervention of a human programmer refer to as automatic patch generation automatic bug repair or automatic program repair the typical goal of such technique be to automatically generate correct patch to eliminate bug in software program without cause software regression at a high level automatic bug-fixing technique generate a patch for a program in two step the first step be patch generation which analyze the original program and produce one or more candidate patch with a variety of technique such search-based program mutation machine learning and genetic programming the second step be patch validation which validate the produce candidate patch from the previous step with either a formal specification or a test suite of the program the generate-and-validate technique be arguably the standard approach to generate repair for a bug of a program such a technique typically start with a test suite of the program i.e. a set of test case at least one of which expose the bug the technique assume that the bug can be fix with a series of mutation operation on the source code of the program it first use fault localization technique to identify suspicious statement in the program it then apply the mutation operation to the identify statement to generate a space of candidate patch and search this space to find validated patch that produce correct output for all case in the test suite generate-and-validate technique for automatic bug-fixing be still in they infancy two earliest generate-and-validate bug-fixing system be genprog and ClearView the effectiveness of generate-and-validate technique remain controversial because they typically do not provide patch correctness guarantee nevertheless the report result of recent state-of-the-art technique be generally promising for example on systematically collect real world bug in eight large c software program the state-of-the-art bug-fixing system prophet generate correct patch for out of the bug target automatic bug-fixing technique generate repair for specific class of error such as null pointer exception integer overflow buffer overflow memory leak etc. such technique often use empirical fix template to fix bug in the target scope for example insert a conditional statement to check whether the value of a variable be null or insert miss memory deallocation statement compare to generate-and-validate technique target technique tend to have better bug-fixing accuracy but a much narrow scope at the patch generation step automatic bug-fixing technique use one or more of the following to generate a set of candidate patch one way to generate candidate patch be to apply mutation operator on the original program mutation operator manipulate the original program potentially via its abstract syntax tree representation or a more coarse-grained representation such as operate at the statement-level or block-level earlier genetic improvement approach operate at the statement level and carry out simple delete/replace operation such as delete a exist statement or replace a exist statement with another statement in the same source file recent machine learning and solver approach use more fine-grained operator at the abstract syntax tree level to generate more diverse set of candidate patch use fix template be a alternative way to generate candidate patch fix template be typically predefined program mutation rule for fix specific class of bug example of fix template include insert a conditional statement to check whether the value of a variable be null to fix null pointer exception insert memory deallocation statement to fix memory leak and change a integer constant by one to fix off-by-one error compare to program mutation technique fix template tend to achieve better candidate patch for bug within its scope fix template be therefore often adopt by target technique machine learning technique can improve the effectiveness of automatic bug-fixing system one example of such technique learn from past successful patch from human developer collect from open source repository in GitHub and SourceForge it then use the learn information to recognize and prioritize potentially correct patch among all generate candidate patch alternatively patch can be directly mine from exist source example approach include mine patch from donor application or from web site another way to generate candidate patch be to use solver for satisfiability modulo theory smt solver-based technique convert a program into smt formula they then query smt solver to solve the convert smt formula to find candidate patch that allow the patched program to pass all supply test case the benefit of this approach be that smt solver can quickly find patch pass test case for small to medium size formula the limitation of this approach be that real world program be often convert to intractably large formula especially for modify statement with side effect at the patch validation step automatic bug-fixing technique rely on either formal specification or a test suite to validate generate candidate patch formal specification specify the correct behavior of a program and be often only available for specific class of error in practice therefore standard generate-and-validate technique typically rely on the availability of a test suite a test-suite - the input/output pair specify the functionality of the program possibly capture in assertion can be use as a oracle to validate candidate patch this oracle can in fact be divide between the bug oracle that expose the faulty behavior and the regression oracle which encapsulate the functionality any program repair method must preserve generate-and-validate approach use automate testing technique to compile and test each candidate patch produce in the patch generation stop and collect all validate patch that produce expect output for all input in the test suite note that a test suite be typically incomplete and do not cover all possible case therefore it be often possible for a validate patch to produce expected output for all input in the test suite but incorrect output for other input the existence of such validate but incorrect patch be a major challenge for generate-and-validate technique recent successful automatic bug-fixing technique often rely on additional information other than the test suite such as information learn from previous human patch to further identify correct patch among validate patch another way to validate candidate patch be to verify the patched program against formal specification which specify the correct behavior of the program verification against full specification that specify the whole program behavior include functionality be less common because such specification be typically not available in practice and the computation cost of such verification be prohibitive for specific class of error however implicit partial specification be often available for example there be targeted bug-fixing technique validate that the patched program can no longer trigger overflow error in the same execution path Automatic bug-fixing technique that rely on a test suite do not provide patch correctness guarantee because the test suite be incomplete and do not cover all case a weak test suite may cause generate-and-validate technique to produce validate but incorrect patch that have negative effect such as eliminate desirable functionality cause memory leak and introduce security vulnerability this weak test suite issue be alternatively call as overfitting of bug-fixing system for example a recent study show that for out Sarcomere sarcomere greek sarx flesh meros part be the basic unit of striated muscle tissue it be the repeat unit between two z line skeletal muscle be compose of tubular muscle cell myocyte call muscle fiber or myofiber which be form in a process know as myogenesis muscle fiber contain numerous tubular myofibril myofibril be compose of repeat section of sarcomere which appear under the microscope as alternate dark and light band sarcomere be compose of long fibrous protein as filament that slide past each other when a muscle contract or relax two of the important protein be myosin which form the thick filament and actin which form the thin filament Myosin have a long fibrous tail and a globular head which bind to actin the myosin head also bind to atp which be the source of energy for muscle movement myosin can only bind to actin when the binding site on actin be expose by calcium ion actin molecule be bind to the z line which form the border of the sarcomere other band appear when the sarcomere be relax a muscle fiber from a biceps muscle may contain sarcomere the myofibril of smooth muscle cell be not arrange into sarcomere the sarcomere be what give skeletal and cardiac muscle they striated appearance which be first describe by Leeuwenhoek the relationship between the protein and the region of the sarcomere be as follow upon muscle contraction the a-band do not change they length micrometer in mammalian skeletal muscle whereas the I-bands and the h-zone shorten this cause the z line to come closer together the protein tropomyosin cover the myosin binding site of the actin molecule in the muscle cell to allow the muscle cell to contract tropomyosin must be move to uncover the binding site on the actin calcium ion bind with troponin-c molecule which be disperse throughout the tropomyosin protein and alter the structure of the tropomyosin force it to reveal the cross-bridge binding site on the actin the concentration of calcium within muscle cell be boil then cut into small cake as staple food replacement of steamed rice the texture be similar to those of ketupat with the difference that ketupat container be make from weave janur young coconut leaf frond while lontong use banana leaf instead it be commonly call nasi himpit light press rice in Malaysia despite actually have different method to create it arem-arem be the smaller size of lontong fill with vegetable carrot common bean and potato sometimes also fill with meat be eat as snack the dish be usually serve cold or at room temperature with peanut sauce-based dish such as gado-gado karedok ketoprak other traditional salad and satay it can be eat as a accompaniment to coconut milk-based soup such as soto gulai and curry it be also use as a alternative to vermicelli noodle Lontong be traditionally make by boil the rice until it be partially cook and pack it tightly into a rolled-up banana leaf the leaf be secure with lidi semat wooden needle make from the central rib of coconut leaf and cook in boiling water for about minute once the compacted rice have cool it can be cut up into bite-sized piece outer part of lontong usually have greenish color because of the chlorophyll leave by banana leaf rub off on rice cake surface alternative way of cooking lontong include place uncooked rice into a muslin bag then let the water seep in and cause the rice to form a solid mass another popular and easier method be by use commercially available plastic pouch rice-filled and punctured with needle to create small hole to allow the water to seep into the package which be then boil until the rice become cook and have fully fill up the pouch this method be mean to imitate the banana leaf liquid permeability nevertheless the use of organic banana leaf be highly recommend for better health and ecological reason on the other hand malaysian nasi himpit light press rice be traditionally create differently the method be more a mechanical pressure than apply permeable boil technique freshly cook rice be compress for a few hour between two heavy stone slab or two tray with a heavy weight on top to produce nasi himpit however nasi himpit be now usually speedily produce in water permeable plastic sachet fill with rice and boil in water just like rice the taste of lontong be bland and neutral it depend on other ingredient to give taste through spice photosensitive compound beneath the skin in some case the photodynamic substance come from ingest plant or drug after be metabolize or not in other case the photodynamic substance may be produce in the body itself due to inborn error in pigment metabolism especially those involve the heme synthesis photosensitivity reaction be usually see in herbivorous or omnivorous animal though such reaction the absence of some key metabolic enzyme the product of intermediary metabolism accumulate they be either eliminate through the urine and body fluid or be deposit in some body tissue such as bone and tooth a common condition see in animal be congenital porphyria due to the accumulation of Uroporphyrin which be deposit in the tooth and bone give they a pink discolouration or excrete through the urine exhibit a pinkish fluorescence under ultraviolet light type iii aka hepatic photosensitivity be the most common type of photosensitivity reaction see in animal in this type the photodynamic substance be phylloerythrin a derivative of chlorophyll produce in the body normally phylloerythrin be secrete into the intestine by the biliary system and excrete through the fece in type iii photosensitivity damage to the biliary transport mechanism prevent the excretion of phylloerythrin allow the photodynamic substance to enter the circulatory system and accumulate under the skin this condition be exacerbate by the presence of hepatic parasite type iv photosensitivity occur follow the ingestion of certain plant such as alfalfa the reason be obscure or idiopathic affected animal Gallagher index the Gallagher index measure a electoral system relative disproportionality between vote receive and seat allot in a legislature as such it measure the difference between the percentage of vote each party get and the percentage of seat each party get in the result legislature and it measure this dis-proportionality from all party collectively in any one give election this collective dis-proportionality from this one election be give a precise score which can then be use in compare various level of proportionality among various election from various electoral system as show on the left side of the equation the Gallagher index use the method of Least Squares or LSq the index involve take the square root of half the sum of the square of the difference between percent of vote formula_1 and percent of seat formula_2 for each of the political party formula_3 the index weigh the deviation by they own value create a responsive index range from to the larger the difference between the percentage of the vote and the percentage of seat sum over all party the larger the Gallagher index the larger the index value the larger the disproportionality and vice versa Michael Gallagher who create the index include other party as a whole category and Arend Lijphart modify it exclude those party unlike the well-known Loosemore hanby index the Gallagher index be less sensitive to small discrepancy the Gallagher index gain considerable attention in Canada in December in the context of effort to reform Canada electoral system the special Committee on Electoral Reform a Parliamentary Committee recommend that the government should as it develop a new electoral system use the Gallagher index in order to minimize the level of distortion between the popular will of the electorate and the resultant seat allocation in Parliament the committee recommend that the government should seek to design a system that achieve a Gallagher score of or less in the canadian when in the presence of other they tend to perform better on simple or well-rehearsed task and worse on complex or new one the Yerkes-Dodson law when apply to social facilitation state that the mere presence of other people will enhance the performance in speed and accuracy of well-practiced task but will degrade in the performance of less familiar task Social facilitation have occasionally be coachbuilding term transfer over to automobile usage since coachbuilder begin make motor car body instead and because customer be familiar with coachbuild term the landau however be not a style that transfer well to the automobile a forward view be generally insist upon by passenger so the half-landau landaulet style become a more popular choice than the true landau the landaulet open over the rear seat but not the front some of these vehicle be inaccurately describe as landaus while some model with landau bar be falsely convey the impression that it be a convertible coupe the Society of Automotive Engineers International define the landau closed-type body with provision for open or folding the rear quarter by use of landau joint which preclude the use of quarter glass in the 1920s and 1930s especially in the United States landau become associate with a simulated convertible in which a fix roof of a sedan with solid rear quarter be cover with fabric or leather and fit with s-shaped side landau bar to make it appear like a convertible top this become the commonly accept definition of landau in north american marketing usage after World War the term fall into disuse however landau become a model name when Nash Motors introduce the Rambler in the new compact car be available during its first year of production only as a convertible landau the Rambler canvas top open from the windshield header all the way to the back and stow in the trunk area this unique convertible design feature steel frame roof rail call a bridge beam around the car door and side window the Rambler strong body structure eliminate the internal brace that be normally need on other open car essentially it be a cabrio coach the term be also use to describe hardtop pillarless body design during the late-1950 the landau term be revive during the there be a trend for make fake convertible by apply vinyl roof on regular car some of these vehicle be call landaus by they manufacturer and many be fit with landau bar on the rear quarter faux cabriolet some use the term Town Landau such as for one of the model in the Ford Thunderbird line this generally mean a wider rear pillar with no rear quarter window or a partial vinyl roof that be apply only over the rear seat area and be thus reminiscent of a town car a landau roof be commonly use on the north american hearse these vehicle have long close rear quarter a vinyl roof and large polished landau bar this have be the preferred hearse style since before World War

divorce in South Africa Divorce or the dissolution of marriage in south african law refer to the termination of a marital union the canceling of the legal duty and responsibility of marriage and the dissolve of the bond of matrimony between a married couple divorce be unlike annulment which declare the marriage null and void divorce require the sanction of a court in a legal process the legal process of divorce may also involve issue of alimony spousal support child custody child support distribution of property and division of debt prior to the come into operation of the Divorce Act in South Africa on July a decree of divorce could be grant by the court either on one of the two common-law grounds adultery or malicious desertion or on one of the two grounds introduce in by the Divorce Laws Amendment Act incurable insanity for not less than seven year or imprisonment of the defendant spouse for at least five year after such spouse have be declare to be a habitual criminal except in the case of insanity these grounds of divorce be base on the guilt or fault principle that be on the assumption that in every divorce action only one of the spouse be to blame for the breakdown of the marriage the other spouse be completely innocent the success of the plaintiff action be thus dependent on proof that the defendant have wilfully commit a matrimonial offence the guilt principle also determine the patrimonial consequence of divorce in that fail a maintenance agreement between the spouse a order for post-divorce maintenance could be make only in favour of the innocent party against the guilty party and the latter forfeit all patrimonial benefit of the marriage if the former apply for a forfeiture order against he or she severe criticism of the shortcoming of the old divorce law lead to a investigation by the south African Law Commission whose report on the matter ultimately result in the enactment of the Divorce Act of the reform of the law of divorce have as its primary objective the formulation of realistic rule for the dissolution of marriage rule which make it possible to dissolve failed marriage in a way that result in the least possible disruption for the spouse and they dependant and that best safeguard the interest of minor child because it be find that a divorce law base on the guilt principle could not attain this objective the old grounds of divorce base on this principle be replace with the ground of irretrievable breakdown of the marriage this be now the main basis for divorce incurable insanity be retain as a ground for divorce but the minimum period of mental illness be shorten considerably while the continuous unconsciousness of one of the spouse for a minimum period of six month be add as a new ground this shift from fault to failure be also reflect albeit to a lesser extent in the statutory provision govern the patrimonial consequence of divorce customary-law marriage whether enter into before or after the commencement of the recognition of customary marriage Act can like common-law marriage only be dissolve by a court order this jurisdiction vest in the High Court a family court establish under any law or a Divorce Court establish in term of section of the Administration Amendment act but which have exactly the same jurisdiction as any High Court under the Divorce Act which govern common-law marriage a decree of divorce may be grant only on one of the follow three grounds the use of the word may in section and of the Divorce Act of raise the question of whether or not the court have a discretion to refuse a decree of divorce even where all the requirement of one of the abovementioned grounds of divorce have be satisfy for example in case where divorce would result in grave financial or other hardship for one of the spouse it have be argue by several writer that it be the intention of the legislature to vest such a residual discretion in the court when this question be consider obiter by the Appellate Division in Schwartz v Schwartz Corbett reject a interpretation of section favour such a discretion and this be confirm and adopt in Levy v Levy neither the power of the court to postpone divorce proceedings in order that the party may attempt a reconciliation nor the provision in the Act which attempt to safeguard the interest of minor or dependent child of the excess supply in economics a excess supply or economic surplus be a situation in which the quantity of a good or service supply be more than the quantity demand and the price be above the equilibrium level determine by supply and demand that be the quantity of the product that producer wish to sell exceed the quantity that potential buyer be willing to buy at the prevailing price it be the opposite of a economic shortage excess demand in cultural evolution agricultural surplus in the neolithic period be theorize to have produce a greater division of labor result in social stratification and class price and the occurrence of excess supply illustrate a strong correlation when the price of a good be set too high the quantity of the product demand will be diminish while the quantity supply will be enhance so there be more quantity supply than quantity demand the occurrence of excess supply either lead to the lowering of the price or unsold supply the latter reflect excess supply lower the price of a good encourage consumer to purchase more and supplier to produce less a disequilibrium occur due to a non-equilibrium price give a lack of balance between supply and demand excess supply be one of the two type of disequilibrium in a perfectly competitive market excess demand be the other when quantity supply be greater than quantity demand the equilibrium level do not obtain and instead the market be in disequilibrium a excess supply prevent the economy from operate efficiently excess supply in a perfectly competitive market be the extra amount of supply beyond the quantity demand as a example suppose the price of a television be $ the quantity supply at that price be television and the quantity demand be television this illustrate that seller be seek to sell more television than buyer be willing to purchase hence a excess supply of television exist indicate that the market be in a state of disequilibrium in this situation producer would not be able to sell all the television they produce at the desire price of $ this will induce they to reduce they price in order to make the product more attractive for the buyer in response to the reduction in the price of the product consumer will increase they quantity demand and producer will not produce as many as before the market will eventually become balanced as the market be transition to a equilibrium price and quantity excess supply in one market can affect supply or demand in another market for example when there be excess supply in the labor market that be unemployment consumer-laborer will be constrain in they disposable income and hence will demand a smaller quantity of goods at any give price this diminish goods demand result from a constraint in another market be know as the effective demand for goods

performance to increase a engine power output economy or durability these goal may be mutually exclusive and a engine may be detun with respect to output work in exchange for better economy or longer engine life due to lessened stress on engine component it have a long history almost as long as the development of the automobile in general originate with the development of early racing car and later with the post-war hot-rod movement tuning can describe a wide variety of adjustment and modification from the routine adjustment of the carburetor and ignition system to significant engine overhaul at the other end of the scale performance tuning of a engine can involve revisit some of the design decision take at quite a early stage in the development of the engine set the idle speed fuel/air mixture carburetor balance spark plug and distributor point gap and ignition timing be regular maintenance item for all older engine and the final but essential step in set up a racing engine servicing of the engine to meet the manufacturer specification tune-up be need periodically as accord to the manufacturer recommendation to ensure a automobile run as expect Modern automobile now calendar annual calendar include feature particular to the year represent and expire at the year end a perennial calendar differ also from a perpetual calendar which be a tool or reference to compute umbrella brand umbrella branding also know as family branding be a marketing practice involve the use of a single brand name for the sale of two or more related product umbrella branding be mainly use by company with a positive brand equity value of a brand in a certain marketplace all product use the same means of identification and lack additional brand name or symbol etc. this marketing practice differ from brand extension in that umbrella branding involve the marketing of similar product rather than differentiate product under one brand name hence umbrella branding may be consider as a type of brand extension the practice of umbrella branding do not disallow a firm to implement different branding approach for different product line e.g. brand extension marketer may increase the chance of success for a new product launch by use a sub-brand name and a parent brand name simultaneously in the article by Howard Pong Yuen lam and other co-author they report the successful case of use two brand name dual branding strategy by practitioner in China for the Minute Maid Orange Pulp juice drink launch a suggestive sub-brand name help consumer recall the key benefit and feature of the new product a suggestive parent brand name communicate the benefit of the product category a dual branding strategy address the problem of use only one brand name for a new product launch after the successful launch of the first new product by a parent brand marketer be able to launch other new product under other sub-brand name in the future to meet different consumer need marketer may use the same parent brand to introduce different product to build scale for the brand and be able to clearly differentiate the different product offering under different subbrand name if a company acquire a brand from another company a marketer may position the acquire brand as a sub-brand under the parent brand if the marketer have define the business scope of the parent brand broadly enough and with a suggestive parent brand name umbrella branding be use to provide uniformity to certain product line by group they under a single brand name make they more easily identifiable and hence enhance they marketability all product under the same corporate umbrella masterbrand provide structure and credibility to other product of the corporation be expect to have uniform quality and user experience e.g. all product carry the parent brand must be of the same high quality standard factor that may determine the impact of umbrella branding include various theory attempt to explain a consumer decision and company can utilize Trade Promotions to increase product visibility and brand awareness with consumer Trade Promotions can also increase a product consumption rate or the average quantity of a product moreover company use Trade Promotions to improve distribution of they product s at retailer and strengthen relationship with retailer lastly Trade Promotions can be leverage to introduce new product gujarati cuisine many gujarati dish be distinctively sweet salty and spicy simultaneously staple include homemade khichdi rice and lentil or rice and mung bean and chaas buttermilk and pickle as side and tomato be use frequently to prevent dehydration in a area where temperature reach °c °f in the shade it be common to add a little sugar or jaggery to some of the vegetable dish and dal the sweet flavour of these dish be believe to neutralize the slightly bland taste of the vegetable the cuisine change with the seasonal availability of vegetable in summer when mango be ripe and widely available in market for example Keri no ras fresh mango pulp be often a integral part of the meal the spice use also change depend on the season Garam masala and its constituent spice be use less in summer regular fasting with diet limit to milk dry fruit and nut be commonplace in modern time some Gujaratis have become increasingly fond of very spicy and fried dish there be many chef who have serve as part of a thali be typically make from milk sugar and nut Dry sweet such as maga and ghooghra be typically make around celebration such as wedding or at Diwali gujarati cuisine be also distinctive in its wide variety of farsan side dish that complement the main meal and be serve alongside it some farsan be eat as snack or light meal by themselves Gujaratis will often refer to dal-bhat-rotli-saak as they everyday meal for special occasion this basic quartet be supplement with additional shaak sweet dish and farsan a festive Gujarati thali often contain over a dozen item dietary rule restrict the permissible combination of dish for example if kadhi be to be serve then a lentil preparation such as chutti dal vaal or mug nus dal will also be include the sweet dish accompany kadhi will likely be milk or yogurt base like doodhpak or shrikhand however a yogurt-based raita would not be serve with such a meal festive meal base on dal will typically have a wheat-based sweet dish like lapsi or ladoo as the sweet accompaniment many gujarati family make and consume moong dal in they diet on wednesday there be established combination of spice that some believe to facilitate digestion that be eat with different food in coastal Gujarat the Kharwa community have develop a cuisine consist of fresh and dry fish common seafood be pomfret khandwas gedada Wutach Valley Railway The Wutach Valley Railway or be one of the most unusual and impressive stretch of railway in Germany it link the town of Waldshut-Tiengen on the Upper Rhine Railway Hochrheinbahn and the border of Baden-Württemberg and Switzerland with immendingen on the black forest railway schwarzwaldbahn because of the twist route of its central section it be popularly know as the Sauschwänzlebahn pigtail line the line be plan in the though construction be not complete until the 1890s and its purpose be at least partly strategic to allow a means for move military supplies around the south of the Black forest the german empire have seize Alsace and Lorraine from the french in the franco-prussian war of 1870-71 a revenge attack in this area from the french or a preemptive strike to prevent one be key issue in german military thinking at the time the normal commercial route along the Rhine pass into swiss territory so could not be use for military purpose the southern section of the line follow the valley of the Wutach river from Waldshut-Tiengen to Weizen part of the town of stühlingen be relatively conventional however the middle section from Weizen to Blumberg involve a approximately meter gain in height and the military authority specify that the line must not have a gradient of more than since there be a need to move heavy military equipment accordingly the line proceed in a series of curve include one complete circle take km of track to travel a beeline distance of km with spectacular large viaduct tunnel and bridge include the only spiral railway tunnel in Germany the track be of standard gauge and be mainly single track the bridge and tunnel be build on a scale to allow eventual doubling of the track though this be never carry out the final section from Blumberg to meet the Black Forest Railway near Geisingen be again relatively conventional the unconventional configuration of the track result in increase fare as ticket price be calculate on the distance travel along the track the line do indeed play a strategic role at various time in its history and its most recent refurbishment in the early be carry out with fund however in the period after the second World War its commercial use decline and section by section passenger service be withdraw though the southern section remain open for freight traffic until after the Deutsche Bundesbahn withdraw passenger service on the central section in a voluntary organization be set up in to re-open it as a museum line under steam traction and it be now a popular tourist attraction there have be a number of initiative to re-open passenger service on the other section of the line as part of a regional transport strategy and since December the northern section have form part of the 3rd ring railway 3er ringzug network of local railway line in the south-eastern part of the Black Forest in the district of Tuttlingen Rottweil and Schwarzwald-Baar the southern section remain out of regular use though the line remain usable

Color appearance model a color appearance model abbreviated cam be a mathematical model that seek to describe the perceptual aspect of human color vision i.e. view condition under which the appearance of a color do not tally with the corresponding physical measurement of the stimulus source in contrast a color model define a coordinate space to describe color such as the and color model Color originate in the mind of the observer objectively there be only the spectral power distribution of the light that meet the eye in this sense any color perception be subjective however successful attempt have be make to map the spectral power distribution of light to human sensory response in a quantifiable way in use psychophysical measurement the International Commission on illumination cie create the color space which successfully model human color vision on this basic sensory level however the color model presuppose specific view condition such as the retinal locus of stimulation the luminance level of the light that meet the eye the background behind the observe object and the luminance level of the surround light only if all these condition stay constant will two identical stimulus with thereby identical xyz tristimulus value create a identical color appearance for a human observer if some condition change in one case two identical stimulus with thereby identical xyz tristimulus value will create different color appearance and vice versa two different stimulus with thereby different xyz tristimulus value might create a identical color appearance therefore if viewing condition vary the color model be not sufficient and a color appearance model be require to model human color perception the basic challenge for any color appearance model be that human color perception do not work in term of xyz tristimulus value but in term of appearance parameter hue lightness brightness chroma colorfulness and saturation so any color appearance model need to provide transformation which factor in viewing condition from the tristimulus value to these appearance parameter at least hue lightness and chroma this section describe some of the color appearance
