cell music the encyclopédie larousse define a cell in music as a small rhythmic and melodic design that can be isolate or can make up one part of a thematic context the cell may be distinguish from the figure or motif the encyclopédie fasquelle define a cell as the smallest indivisible unit unlike the motif which may be divisible into more than one cell a cell can be develop independent of its context as a melodic fragment it can be use as a developmental motif it can be the source for the whole structure of the work in that case it be call a generative cell a rhythmic cell be a cell without melodic connotation it may be entirely percussive or apply to different melodic segment

the ideal of the imitation of Christ have be a important element of both christian ethic and spirituality reference to this concept and its practice be find in the earliest christian document e.g. the hand present a path to the imitation of Christ base on a focus on the interior life and withdrawal from the world the theme of imitation of Christ exist in all phase of byzantine theology and in the 14th century book Life in Christ Nicholas Cabasilas view live one own personal life in Christ as the fundamental christian virtue the word imitate do not appear in the Canonical Gospels but the word imitation of God be ye therefore imitator of God as beloved child and walk in love even as Christ also love you the early Church have little interest in the historical Jesus and this prevent a immediate development of the concept of literal imitation instead the earliest concept of imitation focus on the work of the Holy Spirit self-sacrifice and martyrdom in time this focus change and by the time of Saint Francis of Assisi attempt at literal imitation of Christ be well establish by the 4th century the ideal of the imitation of Christ be well accept and for Saint Augustine it be the the Council of Tribur consider triple immersion in Baptism as a imitation of the three day of Jesus in the tomb and the rise from the water as a imitation of the resurrection of Jesus this period also witness a grow trend towards the denial of the flesh in favor of the soul among the monastic community who see the rebuffing of the physical body as a imitation of the suffering of Christ as a path to a higher level of spiritual achievement in the 12th century Saint Bernard of Clairvaux consider humility and love as key example of the imitation of Christ Bernard argue that the father send he Son Francis of Assisi who believe in the physical as well as the spiritual imitation of Christ Francis view poverty as a key element of the imitation of Christ who be poor at birth in the manger poor as spiritual life as a imitation of Christ with baptism as the first step in the path towards the imitation of a perfect Christ the theme of imitation of Christ continue to exist in all phase of Christ however John Calvin give a prominent place to the imitation of Christ in he writings and work out the ideal of a mystical union with Christ in a way that resonate with the New testament but the Lata region Lata Lāṭa be a historical region of India located in the southern part of the present-day Gujarat state Shakti-Sangam-Tantra a Shakti cult text compose before 7th century ce state that Lata be located to the west of Avanti India and to the north-west of Vidarbha accord to Tej Ram Sharma Lata northern boundary be form by the Mahi River or at time by the Narmada River in the south Lata extend up to the Purna River and at time up to Daman it include Surat Bharuch Kheda and Vadodara accord to Georg Bühler Lata be the area between Mahi River and Kim River and its major city be Bharuch the Lata region be not mention in the earliest of the Puranas or the Sanskrit epic the earliest mention of the region probably come from the writings of the 2nd century greco-egyptian writer Ptolemy the Larike mention by he be identify with Lata by multiple scholar include Sankalia and Sircar the greek name might have derive from lār-deśa lār country the Prakrit form of lāṭa Ptolemy mention that the delta of the river Mophis identify with mahi and barygaza bharuch be located in Larike Vatsayayana in he Kama Sutra of the third century call it Láṭa describe it as situate to the west of malwa and give a account of several of the custom of its people in sanskrit writings and inscription later than the third century the name be frequently find in the sixth century the astronomer Varahamihira mention the country of Láṭa and the name also appear as Láṭa in a Ajanta and in a Mandasor inscription of the fifth century it be common in the later inscription a.d. of the Chaulukya Gurjara and Ráshṭrakúṭa king as well as in the writings of Arab traveller and historian between the eighth and twelfth century Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa mention that Prince Vijaya come from the Sinhapura city in the Lala or Lada region this region be variously identify as Lata in Gujarat or Rarh in Bengal in the gupta-era record Lata be mention as a vishaya viṣaya or district the lāṭa-viṣaya be well-known until the 8th century the Latesvara country mention in some early gurjara-pratihara and rashtrakuta record be probably same as Lata the Chalukyas of Lata rule the region during the 10th and 11th century

Yaxley v Gotts Yaxley v Gotts ch be a english legal case the Court of Appeal judgment be release on June the case deal with whether section of the law of property miscellaneous provision act which require that contract be in write prevent a oral contract from take effect where otherwise a interest would arise by proprietary estoppel yaxley be a self-employed builder who attempt to persuade Gotts to lend he money for the purchase of a building Gotts instead buy the building but agree Yaxley could have the bottom floor in return for renovate the other flat and manage the building after perform the work at he own cost and time Yaxley argue that a oral agreement between himself and Mr. Gotts be to reward he with ownership of the ground floor of the building Gotts fail to convey the title deed in the name of yaxley when the two fall out Yaxley bring legal proceedings as a plaintiff in court the judge in the case take most of the evidence of Yaxley but would not factor in the evidence give by the defendant Gotts in the end the Judge find a oral contract between the plaintiff and defendant exist this entitle the plaintiff to ownership in the form of a year lease on the portion of the structure per the agreement later when Gotts file a appeal the Court of Appeal dismiss Gotts claim that the claimant be entitle only to a portion of interest in the lease
Aboulia Aboulia or abulia from mean will with the prefix - a in neurology refer to a lack of will or initiative and can be see as a disorder of diminish motivation ddm aboulia fall in the middle of the spectrum of diminish motivation with apathy be less extreme and akinetic mutism be more extreme than aboulia a patient with aboulia be unable to act or make decision independently it may range in severity from subtle to overwhelming it be also know as Blocq disease which also refer to abasia and astasia-abasia Aboulia be originally consider to be a disorder of the will Aboulia have be know to clinician since however in the time since its inception the definition of aboulia have be subject to many different form some contradictory Aboulia have be describe as a loss of drive expression loss of behavior and speech output slow and prolonged speech latency and reduction of spontaneous thought content and initiative the clinical feature most commonly associate with aboulia be especially in patient with progressive dementia it may affect feeding patient may continue to chew or hold food in they mouth for hour without swallow it the behavior may be most evident after these patient have eat part of they meal and no longer have strong appetite both neurologist and psychiatrist recognize aboulia to be a distinct clinical entity but its status as a syndrome be unclear although aboulia have be know to clinician since it have be subject to different interpretation from a pure lack of will in the absence of motor paralysis to more recently be consider a reduction in action emotion and cognition as a result of the change definition of aboulia there be currently a debate on whether or not aboulia be a sign or a symptom of another disease or its own disease that seem to appear in the presence of other more well-researched disease such as Alzheimer disease a survey of two movement disorder expert two neuropsychiatrist and two rehabilitation expert do not seem to shed any light on the matter of differentiate aboulia from other ddm the expert use the term apathy and aboulia interchangeably and debate whether or not aboulia be a discrete entity or just a hazy gray area on a spectrum of more define disorder four of the expert say aboulia be a sign and a symptom and the group be split on whether or not it be a syndrome another survey which consist of true and false question about what aboulia be distinct from whether it be a sign symptom or syndrome where lesion be present in case of aboulia what disease be commonly associate with aboulia and what current treatment be use for aboulia be send to neurologist and psychiatrist most expert agree that aboulia be clinically distinct from depression akinetic mutism and alexithymia however only % believe aboulia be different from apathy while % say they be not different and % be unsure yet again there be disagreement about whether or not aboulia be a sign symptom or syndrome the study of motivation have be mostly about how stimulus come to acquire significance for animal only recently have the study of motivational process be extend to integrate biological drive and emotional state in the explanation of purposeful behavior in human being consider the number of disorder attribute to a lack of will and motivation it be essential that aboulia and apathy be define more precisely to avoid confusion many different cause of aboulia have be suggest while there be some debate about the validity of aboulia as a separate disease expert mostly agree that aboulia be the result of frontal lesion and not with cerebellar or brainstem lesion as a result of more and more evidence show that the mesolimbic and the mesocortical dopamine system be key to motivation and responsiveness to reward aboulia may be a dopamine-related dysfunction Aboulia may also result from a variety of brain injury which cause personality change such as dement illness trauma or intracerebral hemorrhage stroke especially stroke cause diffuse injury to the right hemisphere injury to the frontal lobe and/or the basal ganglia can interfere with a individual ability to initiate speech movement and social interaction study have show that 5-67 % of all patient with traumatic brain injury and % of patient with lesion on they basal ganglia suffer from some form of diminish motivation Aboulia have also be associate with amphetamine withdrawal it may complicate rehabilitation when a stroke patient be uninterested in perform task like walk despite be capable of do so it should be differentiate from apraxia when a brain injured patient have impairment in comprehend the movement necessary to perform a motor task despite not have any paralysis that prevent perform the task that condition can also result in lack of initiation of activity a case study involve two patient who suffer from acute confusional state and aboulia be conduct to see if these symptom be the result of a infarct in the capsular genu use clinical neuropsychological and evaluation at baseline and one year later show that the cognitive impairment be still there one year after the stroke cognitive and behavioral alteration due to a genu infarct be most likely because the thalamo-cortical projection fiber that originate from the ventral-anterior and medial-dorsal nucleus traverse the internal capsule genu these tract be part of a complex system of cortical and subcortical frontal circuit through which the flow of information from the entire cortex take place before reach the basal ganglia cognitive deterioration could have occur through the genu infarct affect the inferior and anterior thalamic peduncle the interesting thing about this case study be that the patient do not show any functional deficit at the follow-up one year after the stroke and be not depressed but do show diminish motivation this result support the idea that aboulia may exist independently of depression as its own syndrome the anterior cingulate circuit consist of the anterior cingulate cortex also refer to as Brodmann area and its projection to the ventral striatum which include the ventromedial caudate the loop continue to connect to the ventral pallidum which connect to the vental anterior nucleus of the thalamus this circuit be essential for the initiation of behavior motivation and goal orientation which be the very thing miss from a patient with a disorder of diminish motivation unilateral injury or injury along any point in the circuit lead to aboulia regardless of the side of the injury but if there be bilateral damage the patient will exhibit a more extreme case of diminish motivation akinetic mutism it be well document that the caudate nucleus be involve in degenerative disease of the central nervous system such as Huntington disease in a case study of acute caudate stroke patient % be find to be experience aboulia most of the case where aboulia be present be when the patient have a left caudate infarct that extend into the putamen as see through a ct or scan diagnosis for aboulia can be quite difficult because it fall between two other disorder of diminish motivation and one could easily see a extreme case of aboulia as akinetic mutism or a lesser case of aboulia as apathy and therefore not treat the patient appropriately if it be to be confuse with apathy it might lead to attempt to involve the patient with physical rehabilitation or other intervention where a source of strong motivation would be necessary to succeed but would still be absent the best way to diagnose aboulia be through clinical observation of the patient as well as question of close relative and love one to give the doctor a frame of reference with which they can compare the patient new behavior to see if there be in fact a case of diminish motivation in recent year imaging study use a ct or scan have be show to be quite helpful in localize brain lesion which have be show to be one of the main cause of aboulia a lack of motivation have be report in % of patient with alzheimer disease while depression be also common in patient with this disease aboulia be not a mere symptom of depression because more than half of the patient with alzheimer disease with aboulia do not suffer from depression several study have show that aboulia be most prevalent in case of severe dementia which may result from reduce metabolic activity in the prefrontal region of the brain patient with alzheimer disease and aboulia be significantly older than patient with alzheimer who do not lack Class conflict class conflict frequently refer to as class warfare or class struggle be the tension or antagonism which exist in society due to compete socioeconomic interest and desire between people of different class the view that the class struggle provide the lever for radical social change for the majority be central to the work of Karl Marx and the anarchist Mikhail Bakunin Class conflict can take many different form direct violence such as war fight for resource and cheap labor indirect violence such as death from poverty starvation illness or unsafe working condition coercion such as the threat of lose a job or the pull of a important investment or ideologically such as with book and article additionally political form of class conflict exist legally or illegally lobby or bribe government leader for passage of desirable partisan legislation include labor law tax code consumer law act of congress or other sanction injunction or tariff the conflict can be direct as with a lockout aim at destroy a labor union or indirect as with a informal slowdown in production protest low wages by worker or unfair labor practice by capital in the past the term Class conflict be a term use mostly by socialist who define a class by its relationship to the means of production such as factory land and machinery from this point of view the social control of production and labor be a contest between class and the division of these resource necessarily involve conflict and inflict harm it can involve ongoing low-level clash escalate into massive confrontation and in some case lead to the overall defeat of one of the contend class however in more contemporary time this term be striking chord and find new definition amongst capitalistic society in the United States and other westernized country the anarchist Mikhail Bakunin argue that the class struggle of the work class peasantry and poor have the potential to lead to a social revolution involve the overthrow of ruling elite and the creation of libertarian socialism this be only a potential and class struggle be he argue not always the only or decisive factor in society but it be central by contrast Marxists argue that class conflict always play the decisive and pivotal role in the history of class-based hierarchical system such as capitalism and feudalism Marxists refer to its overt manifestation as class war a struggle whose resolution in favor of the work class be view by they as inevitable under plutocratic capitalism where society be socially divide base on status wealth or control of social production and distribution class structure arise and be thus coeval with civilization itself it be well document since at least european classical antiquity conflict of the order Spartacus etc. and the various popular uprising in late medieval Europe and elsewhere one of the earliest analysis of these conflict be Friedrich Engels the Peasant War in Germany one of the earliest analysis of the development of class as the development of conflict between emergent class be available in Peter Kropotkin in this work Kropotkin analyze the disposal of goods after death in pre-class or hunter-gatherer society and Pinckney Treaty of the second dispute arise follow the Louisiana purchase in the controversy lead to the secession of part of West Florida know as the Republic of West Florida from spanish control in ratify in Britain form the territory of West Florida out of territory it receive from Spain and France in the Treaty of Paris which end the french and indian war the seven year war in this treaty it receive all of spanish Florida from Spain and nearly all of french Louisiana east of the Mississippi River from France find the new territory too big to govern from one capital the british divide it Revolutionary War they do not however specify the boundary of West Florida which have change over the course of british stewardship in the british period West Florida northern border be initially set Citrullinemia Citrullinemia be a autosomal recessive urea cycle disorder that cause ammonia and other toxic substance to accumulate in the blood since the substance also accumulate in the urine the disorder can also be call citrullinuria two form of citrullinemia have be describe both have different sign and symptom and be cause by mutation in different gene citrullinemia belong to a class of genetic disease call urea cycle disorder the urea cycle be a sequence of chemical reaction take place in the liver these reaction process excess nitrogen generate when protein be use for energy by the body to make urea which be excrete by the kidney type i citrullinemia also know as classic citrullinemia usually become evident in the first few day of life affect infant typically appear normal at birth but as ammonia build up in the body they develop a lack of energy lethargy poor feeding vomit seizure and loss of consciousness these medical problem can be life-threatening in many case a milder form of type i citrullinemia be less common in childhood or adulthood some people with gene mutation that cause type i citrullinemia never experience sign and symptom of the disorder type i citrullinemia be the most common form of the disorder affect about one in birth worldwide mutation in the ass gene cause type i citrullinemia the enzyme make by this gene argininosuccinate synthetase be responsible for one step of the urea cycle mutation in the ass gene reduce the activity of the enzyme which disrupt the urea cycle and prevent the body from process nitrogen effectively excess nitrogen in the form of ammonia and other byproduct of the urea cycle accumulate in the bloodstream lead to the characteristic feature of type i citrullinemia the symptom of type ii citrullinemia and usually appear during adulthood and mainly affect the central nervous system characteristic feature include confusion abnormal behavior such as aggression irritability and hyperactivity seizure and coma these symptom can be life-threatening and be know to be trigger by certain medication infection and alcohol intake in people with this type type ii citrullinemia may also develop in people who have a liver disorder call neonatal cholestasis during infancy this condition block the flow of bile and prevent the body from process certain nutrient properly in many case the symptom resolve within a year year or even decade later however some of these people develop the characteristic feature of adult type ii citrullinemia type ii citrullinemia be primarily find in the japanese population where it occur in a estimate one in to individual type ii have also be report in people from east asian and Middle Eastern population mutation in the slc25a13 gene be responsible for type ii citrullinemia this gene make a protein call citrin which normally shuttle certain molecule in and out of mitochondria these molecule be essential for the urea cycle and be also involve in make protein and nucleotide mutation in slc25a13 typically prevent the production of any functional citrin which inhibit the urea cycle and disrupt the production of protein and nucleotide the result buildup of ammonia and other toxic substance lead to the symptom of type ii citrullinemia researcher have find many infant with neonatal intrahepatic cholestasis have the same mutation in the slc25a13 gene as adult with type ii citrullinemia there be multiple treatment method low protein diet be intend to minimize production of ammonia arginine sodium benzoate and sodium phenylacetate help to remove ammonia from the blood dialysis may be use to remove ammonia from the blood when it reach critical level in some case liver transplant have be successful

dike geology a dike or dyke in geological usage be a sheet of rock that be form in a fracture in a pre-existing rock body dike can be either magmatic or sedimentary in origin magmatic dike form when magma intrude into a crack then crystallize as a sheet intrusion either cut across layer of rock or through a contiguous mass of rock clastic dike be form when sediment fill a pre-existing crack a intrusive dike be a igneous body with a very high aspect ratio which mean that its thickness be usually much smaller than the other two dimension thickness can vary from sub-centimeter scale to many meter and the lateral dimension can extend over many kilometre a dike be a intrusion into a opening cross-cutting fissure shoulder aside other pre-existing layer or body of rock this imply that a dike be always younger than the rock that contain it dike be usually high-angle to near-vertical in orientation but subsequent tectonic deformation may rotate the sequence of strata through which the dike propagate so that the dike become horizontal near-horizontal or conformable intrusion along bedding plane between strata be call intrusive sill sometimes dike appear in swarm consist of several to hundred of dike emplace more or less contemporaneously during a single intrusive event the world largest dike swarm be the Mackenzie dike swarm in the Northwest Territories Canada dike often form as either radial or concentric swarm around plutonic intrusive volcanic neck or feeder vent in volcanic cone the latter be know as ring dike dike can vary in texture and they composition can range from diabase or basaltic to granitic or rhyolitic but on a global perspective the basaltic composition prevail manifest ascent of vast volume of mantle-derived magma through fractured lithosphere throughout Earth history pegmatite dike comprise extremely coarse crystalline granitic rock - often associate with late-stage granite intrusion or metamorphic segregation aplite dike be fine-grained or sugary-textured intrusive of granitic composition in contrast to magmatic dike a sill be a magmatic sheet intrusion that form within and parallel to the bedding of layered rock sedimentary dike or clastic dike be vertical body of sedimentary rock that cut off other rock layer they can form in two way

hebbian theory hebbian theory be a theory in neuroscience that propose a explanation for the adaptation of neuron in the brain during the learning process it describe a basic mechanism for synaptic plasticity where a increase in synaptic efficacy arise from the presynaptic cell repeat and persistent stimulation of the postsynaptic cell introduce by Donald Hebb in he book The Organization of Behavior the theory be also call Hebb rule Hebb postulate and cell assembly theory Hebb state it as follow let we assume that the persistence or repetition of a reverberatory activity or trace tend to induce lasting cellular change that add to its stability when a axon of cell a be near enough to excite a cell b and repeatedly or persistently take part in firing it some growth process or metabolic change take place in one or both cell such that a s efficiency as one of the cell firing b be increase the theory be often summarize as cell that fire together wire together this summary however should not be take too literally Hebb emphasize that cell a need to take part in firing cell b and such causality can occur only if cell a fire just before not at the same time as cell b this important aspect of causation in Hebb work foreshadow what be now know about spike-timing-dependent plasticity which require temporal precedence the theory attempt to explain associative or hebbian learning in which simultaneous activation of cell lead to pronounced increase in synaptic strength between those cell it also provide a biological basis for errorless learning method for education and memory rehabilitation in the study of neural network in cognitive function it be often regard as the neuronal basis of unsupervised learning hebbian theory concern how neuron might connect themselves to become engram Hebb theory on the form and function of cell assembly can be understand from the following the general idea be a old one that any two cell or system of cell that be repeatedly active at the same time will tend to become associate so that activity in one facilitate activity in the other Hebb also write when one cell repeatedly assist in firing another the axon of the first cell develop synaptic knob or enlarge they if they already exist in contact with the soma of the second cell Gordon Allport posit additional idea regard cell assembly theory and its role in form engram along the line of the concept of auto-association describe as follow if the input to a system cause the same pattern of activity to occur repeatedly the set of active element constitute that pattern will become increasingly strongly interassociate that be each element will tend to turn on every other element and with negative weight to turn off the element that do not form part of the pattern to put it another way the pattern as a whole will become auto-associated we may call a learn auto-associated pattern a engram hebbian theory have be the primary basis for the conventional view that when Maoist Theory of National Struggle The Theory of National Struggle simplify Chinese 民族斗争理论 traditional Chinese 民族鬥爭理論 pinyin Mínzú Dòuzhēng Lilùn or ethnic struggle refer to one of Mao Zedong political theory on the application of Marxism in China this theory be also Mao Zedong remedy to the National Question in marxist theory as a subset of the general philosophy of Mao Zedong Thought the theory of national struggle address the question of how classical marxist-leninist idea of political economy should intersect with China particular need for construct a multi-ethnic national sovereignty without abandon the universality of Marxism-Leninism the gist of Mao theory be that chinese communist should treat the question of national and ethnic liberation in China as a subset of the larger socialist project of class conflict in strategic term this mean that the key to construct a multiethnic chinese nation-state be to mobilize and transform backward ethnic minority into modern subject of proletariat class consciousness under the leadership of the chinese Communist Party Mao political theory of Nation Struggle work in tandem with he theory of history New Democracy in formulate the history of Modern China as a series of social political economic and cultural transformation mark by a national process of class awakening react against encroachment by western and japanese colonial aggression Mao argue that a national struggle to restore chinese sovereignty be the first vital step in construct a multi-ethnic regime of proletariat dictatorship in do so Mao prioritize the creation of a unite front against foreign aggression as the larger struggle of the chinese revolution one that involve the simultaneous cultivation of a united national identity amongst different ethnic minority group and the transformation of feudal-minded ethnic minority population into modern proletariat subject the amalgamation of Mao two separate theory of revolution signify he theoretical departure from the general doctrine of Marxism-Leninism in Soviet Union and in Europe which strictly hold the economic-determinist ideal that base determine superstructure Mao theory not only address the primacy of nationalism in revolutionary mobilization but also cast doubt on the classical marxist notion of historical inevitability because Mao argue that a nation-wide class consciousness could not be awaken in China unless cultivate by party leadership moreover by conflate the notion of ethnicity and nationality Mao justify the geopolitical claim over the former territory and ethnic minority subject of the multi-ethic Qing Empire since Mao come to power in the communist establishment during the Yan a period Mao theory of national struggle become the guide principle of ethnic and national liberation strategy of the chinese Communist Party until he death in one of the greatest theoretical conundrum in Marxism be the contradiction between internationalism and nationalism the theory and praxis of proletarian revolution in the original Das Kapital Marx offer neither a systematic theory of the national question a precise definition of the construct of the nation nor a general political strategy for the proletariat to seize state power even when Marx do talk about the political implication of the worker state that he envision he article on the subject be for the most part strictly analytical and root in the concrete political case derive from he historical observation due to the ambivalence on statecraft in marxist theory marxist theorist and revolutionary from different region and era generally reinterpret Marx in order to accommodate local demand for national sovereignty under pressure of global capitalist intervention in Lenin theorize that the creation of a national community must start with the unification of the oppressed race and ethnicity to create a worker state against the oppressive race and ethnicity of imperialism in this process of unification Lenin argue that the proletariat must lead the revolution by break through boundary of geo-cultural of difference to reach people who be less enlighten with the ultimate goal of create a communist society under universal proletariat leadership Lenin approach to the classical National Question in also include a specific political strategy of liberation with regard to minority ethnicity in which Lenin claim that the oppressed race and ethnicity should reserve the right of ethnic-self determination once a universal worker state be establish in addition Lenin argue that the principle of ethnic self-determination could prevent the proletariat from be corrupt by capitalist chauvinist who would harness cultural difference and nationalism as a tool to divide the oppressed in the later year of Soviet Union Joseph Stalin would co-opt Lenin approach to the National Question to advance and legitimize he own theory of socialism in one state in East Asia theoretical approach to the National Question be generally center around the notion of ethnic development and national identity as intellectual in China and Japan constantly seek to redefine what it mean to be modern when they traditional cultural subjectivity be threaten subvert and dismember by the colonial west political scientist Germaine Hoston have recently write about the modification and reception of the National Question as it be transport from Europe and Soviet Union to East Asia by the Comintern she argue that in Japan and China the significance of the national question expand beyond the narrow focus of nationality in european Marxism namely the attempt by ethnically distinct population to construct they own national community in the wake of rise transnational class consciousness to include issue such as ethnic development modernization statecraft cultural identity and human agency in China this metamorphism be generally lead by the ccp under the leadership of Mao Zedong althuogh other important theorist also participate in the engineering of theory of National Struggle despite the canonization of Maoism in the people republic of China Mao theory of national struggle be not a monolithic construct that be unaffected by the vicissitude of time neither be Mao the only contributor to China unique marxist political theory of ethnic liberation Historically Mao political theory of National Struggle go through several stage of rhetorical and strategic development under the long March the Yan a Rectification Movement the second Sino-Japanese War the Chinese Civil War and the People republic of China Contemporary scholar of Mao Zedong Thought in the north american academia generally avoid periodize the history of maoist philosophy into strict category of linear development in the chinese academia however the periodization and categorization of Mao Zedong Thought be encourage by the state because it help to establish Mao theory as ideological doctrine in general chinese scholar identify four to five developmental stage of Mao National Struggle Theory the first phase be the Inchoate experimental phase May October in its early phase lead chinese marxist intellectual like Li Dazhao and Chen Duxiu focus on the direct application of classical marxist theory in China derive insight from Karl Marx work on the jewish question and Lenin and Stalin commentary on the National Question these theory espouse the notion that the chinese approach to ethnic and national liberation must closely observe and corroborate the orthodoxy of the New Philosophy in the Soviet Union which be later canonize in the Constitution of Chinese Soviet Republic in before he ascension to political leadership in the chinese Communist Party Mao Zedong holistically embrace this soviet idealogical orthodoxy as the correct approach to the mobilization of ethnic minority in China during the period of Guomindang administration corroborate the dominant soviet thought in the chinese Communist Party Mao second the soviet strategy of ethnic liberation which see the leninist ethnic self-determination and confederate soviet socialist ethnic-autonomy as possible institutional model that China might follow if Communists might seize the power to create a multi-ethnic nation in February Mao write he first piece of ideological literature that directly deal with the problem of ethnicity and national struggle in China in he article name the analysis of Class structure in chinese society Mao identify two revolutionary group in chinese society the peasant and the National Bourgeoisie as potential ally of the chinese proletariat revolution accord to Mao peasant be the most loyal and easily-mobilized subject of the chinese revolutionary cause despite they obsession of commodity-exchange and land due to entrenched semi-feudal petty-bourgeois mentality on the other hand National bourgeoisie be only temporary ally of the proletariat because they major interest be capital accumulation which make they dedicate to the preservation of national sovereignty and ethnic autonomy but not to the ultimate goal of socialist construction nevertheless these embryonic idea of show that Mao have already try to fuse the notion of national and ethnic struggle with the theory of class struggle during the time of soviet theoretical dominance the second phase of theoretical development October July overlap with the period of long March when idealogical hostility toward the Guomindang political theory of sovereignty coincide with the gradual accession of maoist leadership within the Chinese Party during this period of civil warfare Mao nascent political power cement the dominance of he theory within the party leadership which maintain that the project of restore national sovereignty must take precedence before a nation-wide campaign of class struggle in he writings Mao dismiss the theory of Consanguineous Descent and Ethnic Sovereignty by the dominant guomindang chinese nationalist Party regime these dominant theory include the three people ideology by Sun Yat-sen and the racial ideology of Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek Sun Yat-sen political ideal espouse the restoration of han-chinese dominance in China which directly speak to popular anti-manchurian sentiment during the late Qing Dynasty Chiang Kai-shek go one step further by assert that China be a racially and ethnically homogenous nation with han-chinese be the ancestral inhabitant of China and all other ethnic minority be sub-variety of the Han Mao critically reject Chiang theory and label he a fascist and Han Chauvinist for refuse to acknowledge the ethnic difference between han-chinese and other minority Mao theory be also herald by one of the key architect of the party ideology of Maoist think Li Weihan who point out the hypocrisy of Chaing promise of ethnic equality in the kmt national congress with regard to the ethnic education policy of the Hui muslim population in Northwestern China like Mao Li argue that the Hui muslim population be not descendant of the Han people thus the correct way to deal with they ethnic difference be not to impose traditional han culture onto they way of living but to enforce ideological education in order to transform they belief from the islamic religion to the scientific truth of Marxism-Leninism this phase of theoretical development mark Mao practical attempt to reconcile the internationalist rhetoric of marxism-leninism with the desire to construct a multi-ethnic nation-state the third phase be the New Democratic revolutionary phase July October this phase of theoretical development be mark by the consolidation of Mao political theory as the party orthodoxy during the war against japanese Invasion also call the second Sino-Japanese War from 1931-1945 and the subsequent war against the nationalist in the chinese civil war during this period Mao political theory on ethnic sovereignty radically depart from the earlier leninist approach that address the primacy of ethnic self-determination within the framework of soviet socialist Confederation moreover Mao dissent from Stalin approach to the National Question which emphasize the creation of a russia-centric Soviet Union socialism in one country in April the Soviet Union sign the soviet japanese neutrality Pact Japanese 日ソ中立条約 Romaji Nisso Chūritsu Jōyaku also know as the japanese soviet non-aggression Pact Japanese 日ソ不可侵条約 Romaji Nisso Fukashin Jōyaku with Japan two year after the brief soviet japanese Border War as a retaliative reaction against non-aggression treaty with the japanese empire and Stalin diplomatic recognition of Chiang Kai-shek as the head of China Mao abandon the model of ethnic self-determination for the establishment of a unitary chinese nation that would grant ethnic minority partial ethnic autonomy under the han-chinese dominate ccp accord to historian James Leibold Mao new ethnic-autonomy theory necessitate the construction of a new cultural narrative of what China consist of demographically geo-politically and ethnographically Mao search for a nativist unity of the chinese nation lead to the theorization of a transitional phase of revolution that be absent in any other marxist work outside of China in Mao theory of history the stage of New Democracy be a transitional phase of interclass and interethnic unity before the seizure of state power by the chinese Communist Party in term of the political ideal of national struggle and the theory of ethnic relationship Mao propose the in Yan a in during the height of the Second-Sino Japanese War although the ufwd be originally design exclusively to deal with ethnic problem and contrive strategy to mobilize non-party local elite for the war against japanese invasion the shift its strategic focus to the antagonization of kmt and the mobilization of ethnic minority for national unification after the defeat of japanese empire in until the deal exclusively with the question of National Struggle in China with its 9th Department and 10th Department specifically devoted to the regulation of wartime sino-tibetan and sino-uighur China ruling Minzu ethnic group to guide the Mongol Hui Tibetan and other backward minzus toward they collective liberation and to fostoer the right enviornment in which natural assimilation Chinese 自然同化 could forge a new more evolutionarily robust national people this narrative corroborate Mao innovative approach to the National Question which expand the narrow focus on national liberation in european and soviet Marxism to embrace issue as ethnic development state building cultural identity and national sovereignty in China the fourth phase be the Party Orthodoxy phase October May which be a period of ideological radicalization after the chinese communist have seize state power in this period of Maoist theoretical development be mark by the problem that stem from the practical confrontation with the reclamation of Manchuria Xinjiang and Tibet although Mao political theory with regard to the regulation of ethnic minority remain static during this time this period be characterize by a series of political flip-flop accomplishment as well as disaster like the Hundred Flowers Campaign the land reform the collectivization of agriculture the Great Leap forward and the Great famine the most salient ideological crisis during this period be the inconsistency between the theory and praxis of the ccp with regard to local bureaucratic administration ethnic education and cultural preservation specifically these problem entail the paradoxical treatment of ethnic tibetan Uyghurs and Hui muslim people by the chinese Communist Party on the one hand the promise ethnic equality by allow limited degree of cultural autonomy for minority on the other hand the impose ideological education in ethnic school and discourage minority from observe they cultural religious tradition because they have contradict with the conception of Socialist Modernity the theoretical remedy by Mao be to establish a unifying principle of continuous national struggle that be unilaterally apply to each jurisdictional territory of ethnic autonomy as a modification of Mao earlier National Struggle theory this theory argue that the quest for national struggle continue after the establishment of the people republic of China in this be because Mao reason that there be a unequal development of economic mode of production social relation of production and class consciousness between the ethnic minority hinterland and the han-majority urban area in China for example in the conference of the Central Committee in Mao state that some ethnic group in Yunnan region continue to practice tribalism and live in primitive economic condition of production Mao solution to this problem be the criminalization of the practice of ethnic religion accompany by a series of land redistribution campaign and technological experiment direct by sent-down cadre of the Constructions Corps during the prelude to the Cultural Revolution from 1966-1976 the difficulty of maintain China ethnic sovereignty also intersect with the problem of what Mao call the restoration of capitalism Mao unique view of historical materialism render he conclusion that seizure of state power and means of production by the Communists be not the end goal but the beginning of socialist construction have base he revolution on the peasantry the petty bourgeoisie of the countryside accord to Lenin Mao reason that the only way for the nation to secure its path towards Socialist Construction be to usher a perpetual campaign of national ethnic and class struggle even after the Communists have nationalize private capital and control the state apparatus throughout the year of political radicalization the Maoist theory of national struggle gradually diverge from the soviet theory of revolution which be guide by the Leninist principle of national self-determination within the and Leon Trotsky internationalist approach although Mao initially follow Stalin strategy towards the National Question Mao eventually discard that idea when he face a different demographic geography of ethnic identity in China vast multi-ethnic terrain in practice chinese communist under Mao leadership approach the question of Xinjiang Insurrection Tibetan Independence and Hui muslim dissent as problem that challenge the chinese national sovereignty after the establishment of the regime in the theoretical solution by Mao party state be to reduce all of problem arise from the state regulation of ethnocultural difference into a unequal distribution of the force and relation of production the international reception of Mao theory of national struggle range from total rejection to critical appreciation in the United States rightist theorist have criticize Mao theory of national struggle as the classical demonstration of hypocrisy within the socialist rhetoric of liberation other leftist scholar see Mao political theory as a capricious desire to subordinate Marx dialectical historicism in the favor of China particular reality in justification of Mao political power during the Cold War the Maoist theory of national liberation be herald by some french Marxists note perfumery note in perfumery be descriptor of scent that can be sense upon the application of a perfume note be separate into three class top/head note middle/heart note and base note which denote group of scent which can be sense with respect to the time after the application of a perfume these note be create carefully with knowledge of the evaporation process and intend use of the perfume the presence of one note may alter the perception of another - for instance the presence of certain base or heart note will alter the scent perceive when the top note be strongest and likewise the scent of base note in the dry-down will often be alter depend on the smell of the heart note the idea of note be use primarily for the marketing of fine fragrance the term be sometimes use by perfumer to describe approximately scent or the perfumery process to laypeople fragrant material be list by Poucher in order of volatility and be group under respective evaporation coefficient perfume note that range from to top note be otherwise call the head note perceive immediately upon application of a perfume top note consist of small light molecule that evaporate quickly they form a person initial impression of a perfume and thus be very important in the selling of the product the scent of this note class be usually describe as fresh assertive or sharp the compound that contribute to top note be strong in scent very volatile and evaporate quickly although not as saliently perceive the heart and base-note contribute much to the scent in the top note Citrus and ginger scent be common top note they be also call the heart note the scent of a perfume that emerge just prior to when the top note dissipate the middle note compound form the heart or main body of a perfume and emerge in the middle of the perfume dispersion process they serve to mask the often unpleasant initial impression of base note which become more pleasant with time not surprisingly the scent of middle note compound be usually more mellow and round scent from this note class appear anywhere from two minute to one hour after the application of a perfume lavender and rise scent be typical middle note the scent of a perfume that appear close to the departure of the middle note the base and middle note together be the main theme of a perfume Base note bring depth and solidity to a perfume compound of this class be often the fixative use to hold and boost the strength of the lighter top and middle note consist of large heavy molecule that evaporate slowly compound of this class of scent be typically rich and deep and be usually not perceive until minute after the application of the perfume or during the period of perfume dry-down some base note can still be detectable in excess of twenty-four hour after application particularly the animalic and musk note

riparian buffer a riparian buffer be a vegetated area a buffer strip near a stream usually forest which help shade and partially protect the stream from the impact of adjacent land use it play a key role in increase water quality in associate stream river and lakes thus provide environmental benefit with the decline of many aquatic ecosystem due to agriculture riparian buffer have become a very common conservation practice aim at increase water quality and reduce pollution riparian buffer act to intercept sediment nutrient pesticide and other material in surface runoff and reduce nutrient bank stabilization a riparian buffer be usually split into three different zone each have its own specific purpose for filter runoff and interact with the adjacent aquatic system buffer design be a key element in the effectiveness of the buffer it be generally recommend that native species be choose to plant in these three zone with the general width of the buffer be on each side of the stream Zone this zone should function mainly to shade the water source and act as a bank stabilizer the zone should include large native tree species that grow fast and can quickly act to perform these task forest Zone this zone be important as the first line of defense against contaminant it consist mostly of native grass and serve primarily to slow water runoff and begin to absorb contaminant before fluid structure interaction fluid structure interaction fsi be the interaction of some movable or deformable structure with a internal or surrounding fluid flow fluid structure interaction can be stable or oscillatory in oscillatory interaction the strain induce in the solid structure cause it to move such that the source of strain be reduce and the structure return to its former state only for the process to repeat fluid structure interaction be a crucial consideration in the design of many engineering system e.g. aircraft engine and bridge fail to consider the effect of oscillatory interaction can be catastrophic especially in structure comprise material susceptible to fatigue Tacoma narrow Bridge the first Tacoma narrow Bridge be probably one of the most infamous example of large-scale failure Aircraft wing and turbine blade can break due to oscillation fluid structure interaction have to be take into account for the analysis of aneurysm in large artery and artificial heart valve a reed actually produce sound because the system of equation govern its dynamics have oscillatory solution the dynamic of reed valve use in two stroke engine and compressor be govern by the act of blow a raspberry be another such example fluid structure interaction also occur in move container where liquid oscillation due to the container motion impose substantial magnitude of force and moment to the container structure that affect the stability of the container transport system in a highly adverse manner fluid structure interaction problem and multiphysic problem in general be often too complex to solve analytically and so they have to be analyze by means of experiment or numerical simulation Research in the field of computational fluid dynamics and computational structural dynamics be still ongoing but the maturity of these field enable numerical simulation of fluid-structure interaction two main approach exist for the simulation of fluid structure interaction problem the monolithic approach require a code develop for this particular combination of physical problem whereas the partition approach preserve software modularity because a exist flow solver and structural solver be couple moreover the partition approach facilitate solution of the flow equation and the structural equation with different possibly more efficient technique which have be develop specifically for either flow equation or structural equation on the other hand development of stable and accurate coupling algorithm be require in partition simulation in conclusion the partition approach allow reuse exist software which be a attractive advantage however stability of the coupling method need to be take into consideration in addition the treatment of mesh introduce another classification of fsi analysis the two classification be the conform mesh method and the non-conforming mesh method the Newton raphson method or a different fixed-point iteration can be use to solve problem method base on Newton raphson iteration be use in both the monolithic whereas Newton raphson method solve the flow and structural problem for the state in the entire fluid and solid domain it be also possible to reformulate a problem as a system with only the degree of freedom in the interface position as unknown this domain decomposition condense the error of the problem into a subspace related to the interface the problem can hence be write as either a root finding problem or a fixed point problem with the interface position as unknown Interface Newton raphson method solve this root-finding problem with Newton raphson iteration e.g. with a approximation of the Jacobian from a linear reduced-physics model the interface quasi-newton method with approximation for the inverse of the Jacobian from a least-squares model couple a black-box flow solver and structural solver by means of the information that have be gather during the coupling iteration this technique be base on the interface block quasi-newton technique with a approximation for the Jacobians from least-square model which reformulate the problem as a system of equation with both the interface position and the stress distribution on the interface as unknown this system be solve with block quasi-newton iteration of the Gauss Seidel type and the Jacobians of the flow solver and structural solver be approximate by means of least-square model the fixed-point problem can be solve with fixed-point iteration also call block Gauss Seidel iteration which mean that the flow problem and structural problem be solve successively until the change be smaller than the convergence criterion however the iteration converge slowly if at all especially when the interaction between the fluid and the structure be strong due to a high fluid/structure density ratio or the incompressibility of the fluid the convergence of the fixed point iteration can be stabilize and accelerate by Aitken relaxation and steepest descent relaxation which adapt the relaxation factor in each iteration base on the previous iteration if the interaction between the fluid and the structure be weak only one fixed-point iteration be require within each time step these so-called staggered or loosely couple method do not enforce the equilibrium on the fluid structure interface within a time step but they be suitable for the simulation of aeroelasticity with a heavy and rather stiff structure several study have analyze the stability of partition algorithm for the simulation of fluid-structure interaction

Bihu Bihu be the chief festival in the Assam state of India it refer to a set of three different festival rongalus or Bohag Bihu observe in April Kongali or Kati Bihu observe in October and Bhogali or Magh Bihu observe in January the Rongali Bihu be the most important of the three celebrate the Assamese new year and the spring festival the Bhogali Bihu or the Magh Bihu be the one that be all about food the Kongali Bihu or the Kati Bihu be the sombre thrifty one reflect a season of short supplies and be a animistic festival the Rongali Bihu coincide with poi-sangken festival in Thailand and other region of East and South-East Asia the other two Bihu festival every year be unique to assamese people like some other indian festival Bihu be associate with agriculture and rice in particular Bohag Bihu be a sowing festival Kati Bihu be associate with crop protection and worship of plant and crop and be a animistic form of festival while Bhogali Bihu be a harvest festival assamese celebrate the Rangali bihu with feast music and dancing some hang brass copper or silver pot on pole in front of they house while child wear flower garland then greet the new year as they pass through the rural street the three Bihu be Hindu festival with reverence for Krishna cattle Goru Bihu elder in family fertility and mother goddess but the celebration and ritual reflect influence from aborigine southeast Asia and Sino-Tibetan culture in contemporary time the Bihus be celebrate by all assamese people irrespective of religion caste or creed it be also celebrate overseas by the Assamese diaspora community live worldwide the term Bihu be also use to imply Bihu dance otherwise call Bihu Naas and Bihu folk song also call Bihu Geet in a year there be three Bihu festival in Assam - in the month of Bohaag Baisakh the middle of April Maagh the middle of January and Kaati Kartik the middle of October the Bihus have be celebrate in Assam since ancient time each Bihu coincide with a distinctive phase in the farm calendar the most important and colourful of the three Bihu festival be the spring festival Bohag Bihu or Rongali Bihu celebrate in the middle of April this be also the beginning of the agricultural season Bohag Bihu বহাগ বিহু mid-april also call Rongali Bihu the most popular Bihu celebrate the onset of the Assamese New year around April and the come of spring this and jolpan which give the real essence of the season the first day of the bihu be call goru bihu or cow bihu where the cow be wash and worship which fall on the last day of the previous year usually on April this be follow by manuh human bihu on April the New Year Day this be the day of get clean up wear new cloth and celebrate and get ready for the new year with fresh vigor the third day be climate of Argentina the climate of Argentina be a complex subject the vast size of the country and considerable variation in altitude make for a wide range of climate type Argentina have four season winter June August spring September November summer December February and autumn March May all feature different weather condition summer be the warmest and wettest season in most of the country except in most of Patagonia where it be the driest season Winters be normally mild in the north cool in the center and cold in the southern part with the latter experience frequent frost and snow because southern part of the country be moderate by the surround ocean the cold be less intense and prolonged than area at comparable latitudes in the northern hemisphere spring and autumn be these stream glycol typically see in industry include triethylene glycol teg diethylene glycol deg ethylene glycol meg and tetraethylene glycol treg teg be the most commonly use glycol in industry the purpose of a glycol dehydration unit be to remove water from natural gas and natural gas liquid when produce from a reservoir natural gas usually contain a large amount of water and be typically completely saturate or at the water dew point this water can cause several problem for downstream process and equipment at low temperature the water can either freeze in piping or as be more commonly the case form hydrate with co and hydrocarbon mainly methane hydrate depend on composition these hydrate can form at relatively high temperature plug equipment and piping glycol dehydration unit depress the hydrate formation point of the gas through water removal without dehydration a free water phase liquid water could also drop out of the natural gas as it be either cool or the pressure be lower through equipment and piping this free water phase will often contain some portion of acid gas such as hs and co and can cause corrosion for the above two reason the gas Processors Association set out a pipeline quality specification for gas that the water content should not exceed pound per million standard cubic foot glycol dehydration unit must typically meet this specification at a minimum although further removal may be require if additional hydrate formation temperature depression be require such as upstream of a cryogenic process or gas plant lean water-free glycol purity % be feed to the top of a absorber also know as a glycol contactor where it be contact with the wet natural gas stream the glycol remove water from the natural gas by physical absorption and be carry out the bottom of the column upon exit the absorber the glycol stream be often refer to as rich glycol the dry natural gas leave the top of the absorption column and be feed either to a pipeline system or to a gas plant glycol absorber can be either tray column or packed column after leave the absorber the rich glycol be feed to a flash vessel where hydrocarbon vapor be remove and any liquid hydrocarbon be skim from the glycol this step be necessary as the absorber be typically operate at high pressure and the pressure must be reduce before the regeneration step due to the composition of the rich glycol a vapor phase have a high hydrocarbon content will form when the pressure be lower after leave the flash vessel the rich glycol be heat in a cross-exchanger and feed to the stripper also know as a regenerator the glycol stripper consist of a column a overhead condenser and a reboiler the glycol be thermally regenerate to remove excess water and regain the high glycol purity the hot lean glycol be cool by cross-exchange with rich glycol enter the stripper it be then feed to a lean pump where its pressure be elevated to that of the glycol absorber the lean solvent be cool again with a trim cooler before be feed back into the absorber this trim cooler can either be a cross-exchanger with the dry gas leave the absorber or a air-cooled exchanger most glycol unit be fairly uniform except for the regeneration step several method be use to enhance the strip of the glycol to higher purity higher purity be require for dryer gas out of the absorber since the reboiler temperature be limit to 400f or less to prevent thermal degradation of the glycol almost all of the enhance system center on lower the partial pressure of water in the system to increase strip common enhance method include the use of strip gas the use of a vacuum system lower the entire stripper pressure the process which be similar to the use of strip gas but use a recoverable hydrocarbon solvent a expansion in the chest cavity then take place the onset of contraction of the diaphragm which result in expansion of the intrapleural space and a increase in negative pressure accord to Boyle law and trachea before enter the alveolus other muscle that can be involve in inhalation include Hyperaeration or hyperinflation be where the lung volume be abnormally increase with increase filling of Hammerstone in archaeology a hammerstone be a hard cobble use to strike off lithic flake from a lump of tool stone during the process of lithic reduction the hammerstone be a rather universal stone tool which appear early in most region of the world include Europe India and North America this technology be of major importance to prehistoric culture before the age of metalworking a hammerstone be make of a material such as sandstone limestone or quartzite be often ovoid in shape to better fit the human hand and develop telltale batter mark on one or both end in archaeological recovery hammerstone be often find in association with other stone tool artifact debitage and/or object of the hammer such as ore the modern use of hammerstone be now mostly limit to flintknapper and other who wish to develop a better understanding of how stone tool be make hammerstone be or be use to produce flake and hand axis as well as more specialist tool from material such as flint and chert they be apply to the edge of such stone so that the impact force cause brittle fracture and loss of flake for example they be also widely use to reduce the bulk of other hard stone such as jade jadeite and hornstone to make polished stone tool a good example be the hornstone find in the English Lake District use to make polished axis during the early neolithic period and know as the Langdale axe industry hammerstone be use widely in crush mineral ore such as malachite during the chalcolithic period the earliest part of the bronze age and cassiterite prior to smelting of tin Iron ore would have be crush to powder in a similar way during the Iron Age such crush be need to hasten and encourage reduction in the furnace where charcoal be the main reduce agent other example of they use include reduce mineral like haematite to powder for pigment and crush of hard nut such as hazel nut to extract the edible kernel

Isaac Rosenberg Isaac Rosenberg November April be a english poet and artist he poem from the Trenches be recognize as some of the most outstanding poetry write during the First World War Isaac Rosenberg be bear in Bristol the second of six child and the eldest son of he parent he twin brother die at birth Barnett formerly Dovber and Hacha Rosenberg who be lithuanian jewish immigrant to great Britain from Dvinsk now in Latvia in the family move to Stepney a poor district of the East end of London and one with a strong jewish community Isaac Rosenberg attend St. Paul primary school at Wellclose Square St George in the East parish later he go to the Baker Street Board School in Stepney which have a strong jewish presence in he receive a good conduct award and be allow to take class at the art and Crafts School in Stepney Green in December he leave the Baker Street School and in January start a apprenticeship with Carl Hentschel a engraver from Fleet Street he become interested in both poetry and visual art and start to attend evening class at Birkbeck College he withdraw from he apprenticeship in January as he have manage to find the finances to attend the Slade School of Fine Art at University College London during he time at Slade School Rosenberg notably study alongside David Bomberg Mark Gertler Stanley Spencer Paul Nash Edward Wadsworth Dora Carrington William Roberts and Christopher Nevinson he be take up by Laurence Binyon and Edward Marsh and begin to write poetry seriously but he suffer from ill-health he publish a pamphlet of ten poem Night and Day in he also exhibit painting at the Whitechapel Gallery in afraid that he chronic bronchitis would worsen Rosenberg hope to cure himself by relocate in to the warmer climate of South Africa where he sister Mina live in Cape Town the jewish Educational Aid Society of London help by pay the fare after arrive in Cape Town in the end of June he compose a poem on receive news of the War while many write about war as patriotic sacrifice Rosenberg be critical of it from the onset however feel better and hope to find employment as a artist in Britain Rosenberg return home in March he publish a second collection of poem Youth and then after be unable to find a permanent job enlist in the british Army at the end of October he ask that half of he pay be send to he mother in a personal letter Rosenberg describe he attitude towards war never join the army for patriotic reason nothing can justify war suppose we must all fight to get the trouble over Rosenberg be assign to the 12th Bantam Battalion of the Suffolk Regiment a bantam be a designation for man under the usual minimum height of after turn down a offer to apply for a commission to become a lance corporal Rosenberg be transfer first to the South Lancashire Regiment then to the King Own Royal Lancaster Regiment in June he be send with he unit to serve on the western front in France where he arrive on the 3rd of June he continue to write poetry while serve in the trench include break of day in the Trenches return we hear the Larks and dead man dump in December the Poetry Magazine publish he two poem in January
